nodes.statement: First, assume $d = 2$. Let us show that ${\mathscr{F}} \in {\mathcal{A}}_2$. By Corollary~\ref{corollary:a-as-orthogonals} for this we should check that~$\mathrm{Ext}^\bullet({\mathscr{F}},{\mathscr{O}}_X) = \mathrm{Ext}^\bullet({\mathfrak{E}}_{Z_3},{\mathscr{F}}) = 0$. By Lemma~\ref{lemma:hd-stable} the sheaf ${\mathscr{F}}$ is stable. By Lemma~\ref{lemma:hilbert-fz} and~\eqref{eq:hd-inequalities}, we have $\frac1{\ell(Z_3)}h_{{\mathfrak{E}}_{Z_3}}(t) > h_{\mathscr{F}}(t) > h_{{\mathscr{O}}_X}(t)$, hence by semistability \begin{equation*} \mathrm{Hom}({\mathfrak{E}}_{Z_3},{\mathscr{F}}) = \mathrm{Hom}({\mathscr{F}},{\mathscr{O}}_X) = 0. \end{equation*} Similarly, $\frac1{\ell(Z_3)}h_{{\mathfrak{E}}_{Z_3}}(t-1) < h_{\mathscr{F}}(t) < h_{{\mathscr{O}}_X}(t+1)$, hence \begin{equation*} \mathrm{Hom}({\mathscr{F}},{\mathfrak{E}}_{Z_3}(K_X)) = \mathrm{Hom}({\mathscr{O}}_X(-K_X),{\mathscr{F}}) = 0. \end{equation*} By Serre duality on $X$ (note that ${\mathfrak{E}}_{Z_3}$ is locally free and use Proposition~\ref{proposition:serre-gorenstein}) we deduce \begin{equation*} \mathrm{Ext}^2({\mathfrak{E}}_{Z_3},{\mathscr{F}}) = \mathrm{Ext}^2({\mathscr{F}},{\mathscr{O}}_X) = 0. \end{equation*} Since (again by Serre duality and local freeness of ${\mathscr{O}}_X$ and ${\mathfrak{E}}_{Z_3}$) we can have nontrivial $\mathrm{Ext}^p({\mathfrak{E}}_{Z_3},{\mathscr{F}})$ and~$\mathrm{Ext}^p({\mathscr{F}},{\mathscr{O}}_X)$ only for $p \in \{0,1,2\}$, it remains to check that \begin{equation*} \chi({\mathfrak{E}}_{Z_3},{\mathscr{F}}) = \chi(X,{\mathscr{F}}(K_X)) = 0. \end{equation*} The second equality here just follows from $h_{\mathscr{F}}(-1) = h_2(-1) = 0$, and the first follows from Lemma~\ref{lemma:chi-ez-f} and $h_2(0) + h_2(-1) - 2 = 0$. Thus, we have shown that ${\mathscr{F}} \in {\mathcal{A}}_2 \cong {\mathbf{D}}(Z_2)$. Since $Z_2$ is a zero-dimensional scheme, any object in~${\mathbf{D}}(Z_2)$ is isomorphic to an iterated extension of shifts of structure sheaves of closed points in~$Z_2$. By Lemma~\ref{lemma:e-z-small} these sheaves correspond to sheaves~${\mathscr{E}}_z \in {\mathcal{A}}_2$, hence ${\mathscr{F}}$ is an extension of shifts of those. Since ${\mathscr{F}}$ is a pure sheaf of rank equal to~1, we conclude that ${\mathscr{F}} \cong {\mathscr{E}}_z$ for a closed point $z \in Z_2$.
nodes.statement_short: Case d = 2

nodes.name: Show F in A_2
nodes.statement: Let us show that ${\mathscr{F}} \in {\mathcal{A}}_2$. By Corollary~\ref{corollary:a-as-orthogonals} for this we should check that~$\mathrm{Ext}^\bullet({\mathscr{F}},{\mathscr{O}}_X) = \mathrm{Ext}^\bullet({\mathfrak{E}}_{Z_3},{\mathscr{F}}) = 0$. By Lemma~\ref{lemma:hd-stable} the sheaf ${\mathscr{F}}$ is stable. By Lemma~\ref{lemma:hilbert-fz} and~\eqref{eq:hd-inequalities}, we have $\frac1{\ell(Z_3)}h_{{\mathfrak{E}}_{Z_3}}(t) > h_{\mathscr{F}}(t) > h_{{\mathscr{O}}_X}(t)$, hence by semistability \begin{equation*} \mathrm{Hom}({\mathfrak{E}}_{Z_3},{\mathscr{F}}) = \mathrm{Hom}({\mathscr{F}},{\mathscr{O}}_X) = 0. \end{equation*} Similarly, $\frac1{\ell(Z_3)}h_{{\mathfrak{E}}_{Z_3}}(t-1) < h_{\mathscr{F}}(t) < h_{{\mathscr{O}}_X}(t+1)$, hence \begin{equation*} \mathrm{Hom}({\mathscr{F}},{\mathfrak{E}}_{Z_3}(K_X)) = \mathrm{Hom}({\mathscr{O}}_X(-K_X),{\mathscr{F}}) = 0. \end{equation*} By Serre duality on $X$ (note that ${\mathfrak{E}}_{Z_3}$ is locally free and use Proposition~\ref{proposition:serre-gorenstein}) we deduce \begin{equation*} \mathrm{Ext}^2({\mathfrak{E}}_{Z_3},{\mathscr{F}}) = \mathrm{Ext}^2({\mathscr{F}},{\mathscr{O}}_X) = 0. \end{equation*} Since (again by Serre duality and local freeness of ${\mathscr{O}}_X$ and ${\mathfrak{E}}_{Z_3}$) we can have nontrivial $\mathrm{Ext}^p({\mathfrak{E}}_{Z_3},{\mathscr{F}})$ and~$\mathrm{Ext}^p({\mathscr{F}},{\mathscr{O}}_X)$ only for $p \in \{0,1,2\}$, it remains to check that \begin{equation*} \chi({\mathfrak{E}}_{Z_3},{\mathscr{F}}) = \chi(X,{\mathscr{F}}(K_X)) = 0. \end{equation*} The second equality here just follows from $h_{\mathscr{F}}(-1) = h_2(-1) = 0$, and the first follows from Lemma~\ref{lemma:chi-ez-f} and $h_2(0) + h_2(-1) - 2 = 0$. Thus, we have shown that ${\mathscr{F}} \in {\mathcal{A}}_2 \cong {\mathbf{D}}(Z_2)$.
nodes.statement_short: Show F in A_2

nodes.name: Reduce to Ext vanishing
nodes.statement: By Corollary~\ref{corollary:a-as-orthogonals} for this we should check that~$\mathrm{Ext}^\bullet({\mathscr{F}},{\mathscr{O}}_X) = \mathrm{Ext}^\bullet({\mathfrak{E}}_{Z_3},{\mathscr{F}}) = 0$.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to Ext vanishing

nodes.name: Hom vanishing by stability
nodes.statement: By Lemma~\ref{lemma:hd-stable} the sheaf ${\mathscr{F}}$ is stable. By Lemma~\ref{lemma:hilbert-fz} and~\eqref{eq:hd-inequalities}, we have $\frac1{\ell(Z_3)}h_{{\mathfrak{E}}_{Z_3}}(t) > h_{\mathscr{F}}(t) > h_{{\mathscr{O}}_X}(t)$, hence by semistability \begin{equation*} \mathrm{Hom}({\mathfrak{E}}_{Z_3},{\mathscr{F}}) = \mathrm{Hom}({\mathscr{F}},{\mathscr{O}}_X) = 0. \end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: Hom vanishing by stability

nodes.name: More Hom vanishing
nodes.statement: Similarly, $\frac1{\ell(Z_3)}h_{{\mathfrak{E}}_{Z_3}}(t-1) < h_{\mathscr{F}}(t) < h_{{\mathscr{O}}_X}(t+1)$, hence \begin{equation*} \mathrm{Hom}({\mathscr{F}},{\mathfrak{E}}_{Z_3}(K_X)) = \mathrm{Hom}({\mathscr{O}}_X(-K_X),{\mathscr{F}}) = 0. \end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: More Hom vanishing

nodes.name: Ext^2 vanishing by Serre duality
nodes.statement: By Serre duality on $X$ (note that ${\mathfrak{E}}_{Z_3}$ is locally free and use Proposition~\ref{proposition:serre-gorenstein}) we deduce \begin{equation*} \mathrm{Ext}^2({\mathfrak{E}}_{Z_3},{\mathscr{F}}) = \mathrm{Ext}^2({\mathscr{F}},{\mathscr{O}}_X) = 0. \end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: Ext^2 vanishing by Serre duality

nodes.name: Euler characteristic vanishes
nodes.statement: Since (again by Serre duality and local freeness of ${\mathscr{O}}_X$ and ${\mathfrak{E}}_{Z_3}$) we can have nontrivial $\mathrm{Ext}^p({\mathfrak{E}}_{Z_3},{\mathscr{F}})$ and~$\mathrm{Ext}^p({\mathscr{F}},{\mathscr{O}}_X)$ only for $p \in \{0,1,2\}$, it remains to check that \begin{equation*} \chi({\mathfrak{E}}_{Z_3},{\mathscr{F}}) = \chi(X,{\mathscr{F}}(K_X)) = 0. \end{equation*} The second equality here just follows from $h_{\mathscr{F}}(-1) = h_2(-1) = 0$, and the first follows from Lemma~\ref{lemma:chi-ez-f} and $h_2(0) + h_2(-1) - 2 = 0$.
nodes.statement_short: Euler characteristic vanishes

nodes.name: F in A_2
nodes.statement: Thus, we have shown that ${\mathscr{F}} \in {\mathcal{A}}_2 \cong {\mathbf{D}}(Z_2)$.
nodes.statement_short: F in A_2

nodes.statement: Since $Z_2$ is a zero-dimensional scheme, any object in~${\mathbf{D}}(Z_2)$ is isomorphic to an iterated extension of shifts of structure sheaves of closed points in~$Z_2$. By Lemma~\ref{lemma:e-z-small} these sheaves correspond to sheaves~${\mathscr{E}}_z \in {\mathcal{A}}_2$, hence ${\mathscr{F}}$ is an extension of shifts of those.

nodes.statement: Since ${\mathscr{F}}$ is a pure sheaf of rank equal to~1, we conclude that ${\mathscr{F}} \cong {\mathscr{E}}_z$ for a closed point $z \in Z_2$.
nodes.statement_short: Rank one gives F = E_z

nodes.name: Case d = 3 and part (ii) by the dual decomposition
nodes.statement: The case $d = 3$ is treated similarly. The same argument with~${\mathcal{A}}_2$ and~${\mathcal{A}}_3$ replaced by~${\mathcal{A}}_2^\vee \otimes \omega_X^{-1}$ and~${\mathcal{A}}_3^\vee \otimes \omega_X^{-1}$ and~\eqref{eq:dbx} replaced by a twist of~\eqref{eq:dbx-dual} proves part~$(ii)$.

nodes.statement: Let $p_S \colon M \to S$ be a morphism of schemes.
nodes.name: Morphism p_S: M -> S

nodes.statement: For each geometric point $s \in S$ we denote by $M_s$ the scheme-theoretic fiber of $M$ over $s$ and by~$i_{M_s} \colon M_s \hookrightarrow M$ its embedding.
nodes.name: Fibers M_s and embeddings i_{M_s}

nodes.statement: The embedding $s \hookrightarrow S$ is denoted simply by $i_s$.
nodes.name: Embedding i_s

nodes.statement: Assume ${\mathscr{F}} \in {\mathbf{D}}^-(M)$ and $M$ is proper over $S$, and in $(ii)$ and $(iii)$ that $M$ is flat over $S$. \begin{enumerate} \item[$(i)$] If $i_{M_s}^*({\mathscr{F}}) \in {\mathbf{D}}^{\le p_0}(M_s)$ for some integer $p_0$ and all geometric points $s \in S$, then ${\mathscr{F}} \in {\mathbf{D}}^{\le p_0}(M)$. In particular, if $i_{M_s}^*({\mathscr{F}}) = 0$ for all geometric points $s \in S$, then ${\mathscr{F}} = 0$. \item[$(ii)$] If for all geometric points $s \in S$ the pullback $i_{M_s}^*({\mathscr{F}})$ is a pure sheaf such that $H^k(M_s, i_{M_s}^*{\mathscr{F}}) = 0$ for all~$k \ne 0$ and $\dim H^0(M_s,i_{M_s}^*{\mathscr{F}}) = r$ for a constant $r$, then $p_{S*}({\mathscr{F}})$ is a vector bundle of rank~$r$ on~$S$. \item[$(iii)$] If for any geometric point $s \in S$ there is a point $m \in M_s$ such that $i_{M_s}^*({\mathscr{F}}) \cong {\mathscr{O}}_m$, then there is a unique section $\varphi \colon S \to M$ of the projection $p_S$ and a line bundle ${\mathscr{L}} \in \mathrm{Pic}(S)$ such that ${\mathscr{F}} \cong \varphi_*{\mathscr{L}}$. \end{enumerate}
nodes.name: Fiberwise criteria for families over S
nodes.statement_short: Vanishing, local freeness of pushforward, and being a section are detected on geometric fibers of a proper (flat) M over S.
assumptions: ${\mathscr{F}} \in {\mathbf{D}}^-(M)$ and $M$ is proper over $S$
conclusions: then ${\mathscr{F}} \in {\mathbf{D}}^{\le p_0}(M)$
then $p_{S*}({\mathscr{F}})$ is a vector bundle of rank~$r$ on~$S$
nodes.label: lemma:fiberwise

nodes.statement: $(i)$ Let ${\mathscr{H}}^k({\mathscr{F}})$ be the top nonzero cohomology sheaf of ${\mathscr{F}}$; by assumption it is a coherent sheaf on $M$. Let $s \in S$ be a geometric point in the image of the support of~${\mathscr{H}}^k({\mathscr{F}})$ under the map $p_S \colon M \to S$. The spectral sequence \begin{equation} L_qi_{M_s}^*{\mathscr{H}}^p({\mathscr{F}}) \Rightarrow {\mathscr{H}}^{p-q}(i_{M_s}^*{\mathscr{F}}) \end{equation} implies that ${\mathscr{H}}^k(i_{M_s}^*{\mathscr{F}}) \cong L_0i_{M_s}^*{\mathscr{H}}^k({\mathscr{F}}) \ne 0$, hence $k \le p_0$. $(ii)$ Set ${\mathscr{G}} := p_{S*}({\mathscr{F}})$. By base change we have an isomorphism \begin{equation*} H^\bullet(M_s,i_{M_s}^*({\mathscr{F}})) \cong i_s^* ({\mathscr{G}}). \end{equation*} By assumption, the left hand side is a vector space of dimension $r$ in degree $0$. By~$(i)$ we have ${\mathscr{G}} \in {\mathbf{D}}^{\le 0}(S)$. Moreover the spectral sequence~\eqref{eq:spectral} with $M = S$ and ${\mathscr{F}} = {\mathscr{G}}$ \begin{equation*} L_q i_s^* {\mathscr{H}}^p({\mathscr{G}}) \Rightarrow {\mathscr{H}}^{p-q}(i_s^*({\mathscr{G}})) \cong H^{p-q}(M_s, i_{M_s}^*({\mathscr{F}})) \end{equation*} shows that $L_0i_s^*{\mathscr{H}}^0({\mathscr{G}}) \cong H^0(M,i_{M_s}^*{\mathscr{F}})$ and $L_1i_s^*{\mathscr{H}}^0({\mathscr{G}}) = 0$. Therefore, by Serre's criterion the sheaf~${\mathscr{H}}^0({\mathscr{G}})$ is a vector bundle of rank~$r$. Looking again at the spectral sequence, we see that the canonical map ${\mathscr{G}} \to {\mathscr{H}}^0({\mathscr{G}})$ induces an isomorphism $i_s^*{\mathscr{G}} \to i_s^*({\mathscr{H}}^0({\mathscr{G}}))$ for each $s \in S$, hence by part $(i)$ we have an isomorphism ${\mathscr{G}} \cong {\mathscr{H}}^0({\mathscr{G}})$. Thus $p_{S*}({\mathscr{F}}) = {\mathscr{G}}$ is a vector bundle of rank $r$. $(iii)$ By part $(i)$ we have ${\mathscr{F}} \in {\mathbf{D}}^{\le 0}(M)$ and by part~$(ii)$ we know that $p_{S*}({\mathscr{F}})$ is a line bundle. Denote it by ${\mathscr{L}}$. Then replacing the object ${\mathscr{F}}$ by~${\mathscr{F}} \otimes p_S^*{\mathscr{L}}^{-1}$, we may assume that $p_{S*}({\mathscr{F}}) \cong {\mathscr{O}}_S$. We have by adjunction a map ${\mathscr{O}}_{M} = p_S^*{\mathscr{O}}_S \to {\mathscr{F}} \to {\mathscr{H}}^0({\mathscr{F}})$ that restricts to the fiber $M_s$ over a geometric point~\mbox{$s \in S$} as the natural map ${\mathscr{O}}_{M_s} \to {\mathscr{O}}_m$. Therefore, it is fiberwise surjective, hence by part $(i)$ applied to its cone it is surjective on $M$. So, ${\mathscr{H}}^0({\mathscr{F}}) \cong {\mathscr{O}}_\Gamma$ is the structure sheaf of a closed subscheme $\Gamma \subset M$. By the assumption for each geometric point $s \in S$ we have $i_s^*{\mathscr{O}}_\Gamma \cong {\mathscr{O}}_m$. Therefore the map $p_S\vert_\Gamma \colon \Gamma \to S$ is finite and flat of degree~1. By $(ii)$ we have $p_{S*}{\mathscr{O}}_\Gamma \cong {\mathscr{O}}_S$, so it follows that the map $p_S\vert_\Gamma \colon \Gamma \to S$ is an isomorphism. Therefore, $\Gamma$ is the image of a section $\varphi \colon S \to M$ of the morphism $p_S$. The above argument proves ${\mathscr{H}}^0({\mathscr{F}}) \cong {\mathscr{O}}_\Gamma \cong \varphi_*{\mathscr{O}}_S$. Restricting the triangle $\tau^{\le -1}{\mathscr{F}} \to {\mathscr{F}} \to {\mathscr{H}}^0({\mathscr{F}})$ to an arbitrary fiber $M_s$ we deduce that $i_{M_s}^*(\tau^{\le -1}{\mathscr{F}}) = 0$ for any $s \in S$, hence $\tau^{\le -1}{\mathscr{F}} = 0$ by part $(i)$. Therefore ${\mathscr{F}} \cong \varphi_*{\mathscr{O}}_S$.
nodes.statement_short: Spectral sequence for the derived restriction to fibers; base change and Serre's criterion; graph of a section.
nodes.name: Proof of Fiberwise criteria for families over S
Part (i): top cohomology sheaf survives on a fiber
nodes.statement: $(i)$ Let ${\mathscr{H}}^k({\mathscr{F}})$ be the top nonzero cohomology sheaf of ${\mathscr{F}}$; by assumption it is a coherent sheaf on $M$. Let $s \in S$ be a geometric point in the image of the support of~${\mathscr{H}}^k({\mathscr{F}})$ under the map $p_S \colon M \to S$. The spectral sequence \begin{equation} L_qi_{M_s}^*{\mathscr{H}}^p({\mathscr{F}}) \Rightarrow {\mathscr{H}}^{p-q}(i_{M_s}^*{\mathscr{F}}) \end{equation} implies that ${\mathscr{H}}^k(i_{M_s}^*{\mathscr{F}}) \cong L_0i_{M_s}^*{\mathscr{H}}^k({\mathscr{F}}) \ne 0$, hence $k \le p_0$.

nodes.statement: L_qi_{M_s}^*{\mathscr{H}}^p({\mathscr{F}}) \Rightarrow {\mathscr{H}}^{p-q}(i_{M_s}^*{\mathscr{F}})
nodes.name: Equation (34) spectral
nodes.label: eq:spectral

nodes.name: Part (ii): pushforward is a vector bundle
nodes.statement: $(ii)$ Set ${\mathscr{G}} := p_{S*}({\mathscr{F}})$. By base change we have an isomorphism \begin{equation*} H^\bullet(M_s,i_{M_s}^*({\mathscr{F}})) \cong i_s^* ({\mathscr{G}}). \end{equation*} By assumption, the left hand side is a vector space of dimension $r$ in degree $0$. By~$(i)$ we have ${\mathscr{G}} \in {\mathbf{D}}^{\le 0}(S)$. Moreover the spectral sequence~\eqref{eq:spectral} with $M = S$ and ${\mathscr{F}} = {\mathscr{G}}$ \begin{equation*} L_q i_s^* {\mathscr{H}}^p({\mathscr{G}}) \Rightarrow {\mathscr{H}}^{p-q}(i_s^*({\mathscr{G}})) \cong H^{p-q}(M_s, i_{M_s}^*({\mathscr{F}})) \end{equation*} shows that $L_0i_s^*{\mathscr{H}}^0({\mathscr{G}}) \cong H^0(M,i_{M_s}^*{\mathscr{F}})$ and $L_1i_s^*{\mathscr{H}}^0({\mathscr{G}}) = 0$. Therefore, by Serre's criterion the sheaf~${\mathscr{H}}^0({\mathscr{G}})$ is a vector bundle of rank~$r$. Looking again at the spectral sequence, we see that the canonical map ${\mathscr{G}} \to {\mathscr{H}}^0({\mathscr{G}})$ induces an isomorphism $i_s^*{\mathscr{G}} \to i_s^*({\mathscr{H}}^0({\mathscr{G}}))$ for each $s \in S$, hence by part $(i)$ we have an isomorphism ${\mathscr{G}} \cong {\mathscr{H}}^0({\mathscr{G}})$. Thus $p_{S*}({\mathscr{F}}) = {\mathscr{G}}$ is a vector bundle of rank $r$.
nodes.statement_short: Part (ii): pushforward is a vector bundle

nodes.name: Part (iii): F is the pushforward of a line bundle along a section
nodes.statement: $(iii)$ By part $(i)$ we have ${\mathscr{F}} \in {\mathbf{D}}^{\le 0}(M)$ and by part~$(ii)$ we know that $p_{S*}({\mathscr{F}})$ is a line bundle. Denote it by ${\mathscr{L}}$. Then replacing the object ${\mathscr{F}}$ by~${\mathscr{F}} \otimes p_S^*{\mathscr{L}}^{-1}$, we may assume that $p_{S*}({\mathscr{F}}) \cong {\mathscr{O}}_S$. We have by adjunction a map ${\mathscr{O}}_{M} = p_S^*{\mathscr{O}}_S \to {\mathscr{F}} \to {\mathscr{H}}^0({\mathscr{F}})$ that restricts to the fiber $M_s$ over a geometric point~\mbox{$s \in S$} as the natural map ${\mathscr{O}}_{M_s} \to {\mathscr{O}}_m$. Therefore, it is fiberwise surjective, hence by part $(i)$ applied to its cone it is surjective on $M$. So, ${\mathscr{H}}^0({\mathscr{F}}) \cong {\mathscr{O}}_\Gamma$ is the structure sheaf of a closed subscheme $\Gamma \subset M$. By the assumption for each geometric point $s \in S$ we have $i_s^*{\mathscr{O}}_\Gamma \cong {\mathscr{O}}_m$. Therefore the map $p_S\vert_\Gamma \colon \Gamma \to S$ is finite and flat of degree~1. By $(ii)$ we have $p_{S*}{\mathscr{O}}_\Gamma \cong {\mathscr{O}}_S$, so it follows that the map $p_S\vert_\Gamma \colon \Gamma \to S$ is an isomorphism. Therefore, $\Gamma$ is the image of a section $\varphi \colon S \to M$ of the morphism $p_S$. The above argument proves ${\mathscr{H}}^0({\mathscr{F}}) \cong {\mathscr{O}}_\Gamma \cong \varphi_*{\mathscr{O}}_S$. Restricting the triangle $\tau^{\le -1}{\mathscr{F}} \to {\mathscr{F}} \to {\mathscr{H}}^0({\mathscr{F}})$ to an arbitrary fiber $M_s$ we deduce that $i_{M_s}^*(\tau^{\le -1}{\mathscr{F}}) = 0$ for any $s \in S$, hence $\tau^{\le -1}{\mathscr{F}} = 0$ by part $(i)$. Therefore ${\mathscr{F}} \cong \varphi_*{\mathscr{O}}_S$.
nodes.statement_short: Part (iii): F is the pushforward of a line bundle along a section

nodes.statement: Let $X$ be a sextic du Val del Pezzo surface over an algebraically closed field ${\mathsf{k}}$. The moduli spaces ${\mathscr{M}}_2(X)$, ${\mathscr{M}}_3(X)$, and ${\mathscr{M}}_4(X)$ are fine moduli spaces. Moreover, \newline$(i)$ ${\mathscr{M}}_2(X) \cong {\mathscr{M}}_4(X) \cong Z_2$ and the sheaves ${\mathscr{E}}_{Z_2}$ and ${\mathscr{E}}_{Z_2}^\vee \otimes \omega_X^{-1}$ are the corresponding universal families; \newline$(ii)$ ${\mathscr{M}}_3(X) \cong Z_3$ and the sheaves ${\mathscr{E}}_{Z_3}$ and ${\mathscr{E}}_{Z_3}^\vee \otimes \omega_X^{-1}$ are two universal families for this moduli problem.
nodes.name: Moduli spaces M_d(X) are the schemes Z_d
nodes.statement_short: M_2(X) = M_4(X) = Z_2 and M_3(X) = Z_3 are fine moduli spaces with universal families E_{Z_d} and twisted duals.
assumptions: $X$ be a sextic du Val del Pezzo surface over an algebraically closed field ${\mathsf{k}}$
conclusions: The moduli spaces ${\mathscr{M}}_2(X)$, ${\mathscr{M}}_3(X)$, and ${\mathscr{M}}_4(X)$ are fine moduli spaces
${\mathscr{M}}_2(X) \cong {\mathscr{M}}_4(X) \cong Z_2$
${\mathscr{M}}_3(X) \cong Z_3$
nodes.label: theorem:moduli

nodes.statement: Let $S$ be an arbitrary base scheme and ${\mathscr{F}}$ a coherent sheaf on $X \times S$ flat over $S$ and such that for any geometric point $s \in S$ the restriction ${\mathscr{F}}_s = i_{X \times s}^*({\mathscr{F}})$ is a semistable (i.e., torsion free) sheaf with Hilbert polynomial~$h_d(t)$ for $d \in \{2,3\}$. By Lemma~\ref{lemma:md-points} it follows that \begin{equation*} {\mathscr{F}}_s \cong {\mathscr{E}}_z \end{equation*} for a unique closed point $z \in Z_d$. Consider the semiorthogonal decomposition \begin{equation} {\mathbf{D}}(X \times S) = \langle {\mathcal{A}}_{1S}, {\mathcal{A}}_{2S}, {\mathcal{A}}_{3S} \rangle = \langle {\mathbf{D}}(S), {\mathbf{D}}(Z_2 \times S), {\mathbf{D}}(Z_3 \times S) \rangle, \end{equation} obtained by the base change $S \to \mathrm{Spec}({\mathsf{k}})$ (\cite[Theorem~5.6]{kuznetsov2011base}) from~\eqref{eq:dbx-dz} (the second equality follows from \cite[Theorem~6.4]{kuznetsov2011base} and Proposition~\ref{proposition:fm-zd}). Since by Proposition~\ref{proposition:fm-zd} the embedding functors of~\eqref{eq:dbx-dz} are the Fourier--Mukai functors given by the sheaves ${\mathscr{E}}_{Z_d}$, the embedding functors of~\eqref{eq:dbx-s} are given by the pullbacks ${\mathscr{E}}_{Z_d} \boxtimes {\mathscr{O}}_S$ of ${\mathscr{E}}_{Z_d}$ via the maps $X \times Z_d \times S \to X \times Z_d$. For any ${\mathscr{F}} \in {\mathbf{D}}(X \times S)$, a geometric point $s \in S$, and each $d' \in \{1,2,3\}$ we have by~\cite[(11)]{kuznetsov2011base} an isomorphism \begin{equation*} i_{Z_{d'} \times s}^*(\alpha_{d'S}({\mathscr{F}})) \cong \alpha_{d'}(i_{X \times s}^*({\mathscr{F}})) \in {\mathbf{D}}(Z_{d'}), \end{equation*} where $\alpha_{d'} \colon {\mathbf{D}}(X) \to {\mathbf{D}}(Z_{d'})$ and $\alpha_{d'S} \colon {\mathbf{D}}(X \times S) \to {\mathbf{D}}(Z_{d'} \times S)$ are the projection functors of the semiorthogonal decompositions~\eqref{eq:dbx-dz} and~\eqref{eq:dbx-s} respectively. Using this isomorphism for the sheaf~${\mathscr{F}}$ we started with, and taking into account Lemma~\ref{lemma:e-z-small}, we conclude that \begin{equation*} i_{Z_{d'} \times s}^*(\alpha_{d'S}({\mathscr{F}})) \cong \alpha_{d'}({\mathscr{F}}_s) \cong \alpha_{d'}({\mathscr{E}}_z) \cong \begin{cases} {\mathscr{O}}_z, & \text{if $d' = d$},\\ 0, & \text{otherwise}. \end{cases} \end{equation*} By Lemma~\ref{lemma:fiberwise}$(i)$ it follows that $\alpha_{d'S}({\mathscr{F}}) = 0$ when $d' \ne d$, hence \begin{equation*} {\mathscr{F}} \cong \Phi_{{\mathscr{E}}_{Z_d} \boxtimes {\mathscr{O}}_S}({\mathscr{F}}_d) \end{equation*} for some object ${\mathscr{F}}_d \in {\mathbf{D}}(Z_d \times S)$. Moreover, the object ${\mathscr{F}}_d$ is such that for any geometric point~$s \in S$ we have $i_{Z_d \times s}^*({\mathscr{F}}_d) \cong {\mathscr{O}}_z$ for some closed point~$z \in Z_d$. By Lemma~\ref{lemma:fiberwise}$(iii)$ it follows that ${\mathscr{F}}_d \cong \Gamma_{f_d*}{\mathscr{L}}$, where $f_d \colon S \to Z_d$ is a morphism, $\Gamma_{f_d} \colon S \to Z_d \times S$ is its graph, and ${\mathscr{L}}$ is a line bundle on $S$. Therefore \begin{equation*} {\mathscr{F}} \cong \Phi_{{\mathscr{E}}_{Z_d} \boxtimes {\mathscr{O}}_S}(\Gamma_{f_d*}{\mathscr{L}}) \cong (\mathrm{id}_X \times f_d)^*{\mathscr{E}}_{Z_d} \otimes p_S^*{\mathscr{L}}. \end{equation*} This precisely means that the moduli functor ${\mathscr{M}}_d(X)$ we are interested in is represented by the scheme~$Z_d$, and that ${\mathscr{E}}_{Z_d}$ is a universal sheaf. This proves the statement about~${\mathscr{M}}_2(X)$ and the first statement about~${\mathscr{M}}_3(X)$. The same argument applied to the dual semiorthogonal decomposition~\eqref{eq:dbx-dual} instead of~\eqref{eq:dbx-dz} proves the statement about~${\mathscr{M}}_4(X)$ and the second statement about~${\mathscr{M}}_3(X)$.
nodes.statement_short: Use the base-changed decomposition of D(X x S) and fiberwise criteria to show every family is pulled back from Z_d.
nodes.name: Proof of Moduli spaces M_d(X) are the schemes Z_d

nodes.name: Projection functors commute with restriction to fibers
nodes.statement: For any ${\mathscr{F}} \in {\mathbf{D}}(X \times S)$, a geometric point $s \in S$, and each $d' \in \{1,2,3\}$ we have by~\cite[(11)]{kuznetsov2011base} an isomorphism \begin{equation*} i_{Z_{d'} \times s}^*(\alpha_{d'S}({\mathscr{F}})) \cong \alpha_{d'}(i_{X \times s}^*({\mathscr{F}})) \in {\mathbf{D}}(Z_{d'}), \end{equation*} where $\alpha_{d'} \colon {\mathbf{D}}(X) \to {\mathbf{D}}(Z_{d'})$ and $\alpha_{d'S} \colon {\mathbf{D}}(X \times S) \to {\mathbf{D}}(Z_{d'} \times S)$ are the projection functors of the semiorthogonal decompositions~\eqref{eq:dbx-dz} and~\eqref{eq:dbx-s} respectively.
nodes.statement_short: Projection functors commute with restriction to fibers

nodes.statement: By Lemma~\ref{lemma:fiberwise}$(i)$ it follows that $\alpha_{d'S}({\mathscr{F}}) = 0$ when $d' \ne d$, hence \begin{equation*} {\mathscr{F}} \cong \Phi_{{\mathscr{E}}_{Z_d} \boxtimes {\mathscr{O}}_S}({\mathscr{F}}_d) \end{equation*} for some object ${\mathscr{F}}_d \in {\mathbf{D}}(Z_d \times S)$.

nodes.name: F_d is a graph pushforward of a line bundle
nodes.statement: Moreover, the object ${\mathscr{F}}_d$ is such that for any geometric point~$s \in S$ we have $i_{Z_d \times s}^*({\mathscr{F}}_d) \cong {\mathscr{O}}_z$ for some closed point~$z \in Z_d$. By Lemma~\ref{lemma:fiberwise}$(iii)$ it follows that ${\mathscr{F}}_d \cong \Gamma_{f_d*}{\mathscr{L}}$, where $f_d \colon S \to Z_d$ is a morphism, $\Gamma_{f_d} \colon S \to Z_d \times S$ is its graph, and ${\mathscr{L}}$ is a line bundle on $S$. Therefore \begin{equation*} {\mathscr{F}} \cong \Phi_{{\mathscr{E}}_{Z_d} \boxtimes {\mathscr{O}}_S}(\Gamma_{f_d*}{\mathscr{L}}) \cong (\mathrm{id}_X \times f_d)^*{\mathscr{E}}_{Z_d} \otimes p_S^*{\mathscr{L}}. \end{equation*}

nodes.statement: For the first part of~$(i)$, by Lemma~\ref{lemma:md-points}$(ii)$ it is enough to show that $I_C \otimes \omega_X^{-1}$ is stable with Hilbert polynomial~$h_{6-d}(t)$. Stability is clear by Lemma~\ref{lemma:hd-stable}, and the Hilbert polynomial evidently equals \begin{equation*} h_{{\mathscr{O}}_X}(t+1) - h'_d(t+1) = (3(t+1)(t+2) + 1) - (d(t+1) + 1) = (3t + 6 - d)(t + 1) = h_{6-d}(t). \end{equation*} For the first part of~$(ii)$ first note that by Serre duality \begin{equation*} \mathrm{Ext}^\bullet({\mathscr{O}}_L,{\mathscr{O}}_X) \cong \mathrm{Ext}^\bullet({\mathscr{O}}_X,{\mathscr{O}}_L(K_X))^\vee = H^\bullet(L,{\mathscr{O}}_L(-1)) = 0 \end{equation*} since $L \cong {\mathbb{P}}^1$ and $L \cdot K_X = -1$. Thus by Theorem~\ref{theorem:dbx} the structure sheaf ${\mathscr{O}}_L$ is contained in the subcategory~$\langle {\mathcal{A}}_2, {\mathcal{A}}_3 \rangle$ of ${\mathbf{D}}(X)$. Next, again by Serre duality \begin{equation*} \mathrm{Ext}^i({\mathscr{O}}_L,{\mathfrak{E}}_{Z_2}) \cong \mathrm{Ext}^{2-i}({\mathfrak{E}}_{Z_2},{\mathscr{O}}_L(K_X))^\vee. \end{equation*} Since ${\mathfrak{E}}_{Z_2}$ is a vector bundle and $L$ is a curve, the right hand side is zero unless $i \in \{1, 2\}$. On the other hand, ${\mathfrak{E}}_{Z_2}$ is globally generated by Proposition~\ref{proposition:e-z-big} and~\eqref{eq:cezd}, while ${\mathscr{O}}_L(K_X) \cong {\mathscr{O}}_L(-1)$ has no global sections, hence for $i = 2$ the right hand side is also zero. On the other hand, by Lemma~\ref{lemma:chi-ez-f} we have \begin{equation*} \chi({\mathfrak{E}}_{Z_2},{\mathscr{O}}_L(K_X)) = 2\chi(X,{\mathscr{O}}_L(K_X)) + \chi(X,{\mathscr{O}}_L(2K_X)) - 3r({\mathscr{O}}_L(K_X)) = 2 \cdot h'_1(-1) + h'_1(-2) = -1, \end{equation*} and we conclude that $\mathrm{Ext}^\bullet({\mathscr{O}}_L, {\mathfrak{E}}_{Z_2}) = {\mathsf{k}}[-1]$. This means that there is a unique closed point $z_2 \in Z_2$ and a unique extension \begin{equation*} 0 \to {\mathscr{E}}_{z_2} \to {\mathscr{F}} \to {\mathscr{O}}_L \to 0 \end{equation*} such that ${\mathscr{F}} \in {\mathcal{A}}_3$. It remains to note that ${\mathscr{F}}$ is a sheaf of rank 1, hence there is a unique $z_3 \in Z_3$ such that ${\mathscr{F}} \cong {\mathscr{E}}_{z_3}$. The converse statements are evident.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to Lemma md-points via stability and Hilbert polynomial; for lines compute Ext with E_{Z_2} by Serre duality and Euler characteristic.

nodes.statement: Assume $d \in \{2,3\}$. Let ${\mathscr{C}} \subset X \times S$ be a flat $S$-family of subschemes in $X$ with Hilbert polynomial~$h'_d(t)$. Consider the decomposition of the structure sheaf ${\mathscr{O}}_{\mathscr{C}} \in {\mathbf{D}}(X \times S)$ with respect to the semiorthogonal decomposition \begin{equation*} {\mathbf{D}}(X \times S) = \langle {\mathcal{A}}_{3S}^\vee, {\mathcal{A}}_{2S}^\vee, {\mathcal{A}}_{1S}^\vee \rangle, \end{equation*} obtained from the decomposition of Proposition~\ref{proposition:dbx-dual} by the base change $S \to \mathrm{Spec}({\mathsf{k}})$ via~\cite[Theorem~5.6]{kuznetsov2011base}. The argument of Theorem~\ref{theorem:moduli} together with the result of Lemma~\ref{lemma:oc-decomposition}$(i)$ shows that there is a morphism $f_d \colon S \to Z_d$, a line bundle ${\mathscr{F}}_d$ on $S$, and an exact sequence \begin{equation*} 0 \to (\mathrm{id}_X \times f_d)^*({\mathscr{E}}_{Z_d}^\vee) \otimes p_S^*({\mathscr{F}}_d) \to {\mathscr{O}}_{X \times S} \to {\mathscr{O}}_{\mathscr{C}} \to 0 \end{equation*} The left arrow corresponds to a global section of the bundle $(\mathrm{id}_X \times f_d)^*({\mathscr{E}}_{Z_d}) \otimes p_S^*({\mathscr{F}}_d^\vee)$, i.e., to a morphism from $p_S^*{\mathscr{F}}_d$ to $(\mathrm{id}_X \times f_d)^*({\mathscr{E}}_{Z_d})$. We have \begin{equation*} \mathrm{Hom}(p_S^*{\mathscr{F}}_d,(\mathrm{id}_X \times f_d)^*({\mathscr{E}}_{Z_d})) \cong \mathrm{Hom}({\mathscr{F}}_d,p_{S*}((\mathrm{id}_X \times f_d)^*({\mathscr{E}}_{Z_d}))) \cong \mathrm{Hom}({\mathscr{F}}_d,f_d^*p_{d*}({\mathscr{E}}_{Z_d})), \end{equation*} where the first equality follows from adjunction and the second is the base change for the diagram \begin{equation*} \xymatrix@C=5em{ X \times S \ar[r]^-{\mathrm{id}_X \times f_d} \ar[d]_{p_S} & X \times Z_d \ar[d]^{p_d} \\ S \ar[r]^-{f_d} & Z_d } \end{equation*} The flatness over $S$ of the cokernel ${\mathscr{O}}_{\mathscr{C}}$ of the morphism $(\mathrm{id}_X \times f_d)^*({\mathscr{E}}_{Z_d}^\vee) \otimes p_S^*({\mathscr{F}}_d) \to {\mathscr{O}}_{X \times S}$ is equivalent to the corresponding morphism ${\mathscr{F}}_d \to f_d^*p_{d*}{\mathscr{E}}_{Z_d}$ being nonzero for every closed point $s \in S$. Thus the Hilbert scheme functor $F_d(X)$ is isomorphic to the functor that associates to a scheme $S$ a morphism $f_d \colon S \to Z_d$ and a line subbundle in $f_d^*p_{d*}{\mathscr{E}}_{Z_d}$, hence is represented by the projective bundle ${\mathbb{P}}_{Z_d}(p_{d*}{\mathscr{E}}_{Z_d})$. Now assume $d = 1$ and let ${\mathscr{C}} \subset X \times S$ be a flat family of lines. Decomposing ${\mathscr{O}}_{\mathscr{C}}$ with respect to~\eqref{eq:dbx-s} and using the argument of Theorem~\ref{theorem:moduli} together with the result of Lemma~\ref{lemma:oc-decomposition}$(ii)$, we conclude that there are morphisms $f_2 \colon S \to Z_2$ and $f_3 \colon S \to Z_3$, line bundles ${\mathscr{F}}_2$ and ${\mathscr{F}}_3$ on $S$, and an exact sequence \begin{equation} 0 \to (\mathrm{id}_X \times f_{2})^*({\mathscr{E}}_{Z_2}) \otimes p_S^*({\mathscr{F}}_2) \to (\mathrm{id}_X \times f_{3})^*({\mathscr{E}}_{Z_3}) \otimes p_S^*({\mathscr{F}}_3) \to {\mathscr{O}}_{\mathscr{C}} \to 0. \end{equation} Moreover, the pushforward to $S$ of this sequence gives (again by base change) an exact sequence \begin{equation*} 0 \to f_{2}^*(p_{2*}{\mathscr{E}}_{Z_2}) \otimes {\mathscr{F}}_2 \to f_{3}^*(p_{3*}{\mathscr{E}}_{Z_3}) \otimes {\mathscr{F}}_3 \to {\mathscr{O}}_S \to 0. \end{equation*} Since by Lemma~\ref{lemma:ps-ez} we know that $f_{d}^*(p_{d*}{\mathscr{E}}_{Z_d})$ is a vector bundle of rank $d$ on $S$, the comparison of determinants gives a relation \begin{equation} {\mathscr{F}}_3^3 \otimes {\mathscr{F}}_2^{-2} \cong f_{2}^*(\det(p_{2*}{\mathscr{E}}_{Z_2})) \otimes f_{3}^*(\det(p_{3*}{\mathscr{E}}_{Z_3})^{-1}). \end{equation} Denoting by $f_{23} \colon S \to Z_2 \times Z_3$ the map induced by $f_2$ and $f_3$, we deduce by adjunction and base change \begin{equation*} \mathrm{Hom}(f_{2}^*(p_{2*}{\mathscr{E}}_{Z_2}) \otimes {\mathscr{F}}_2, f_{3}^*(p_{3*}{\mathscr{E}}_{Z_3}) \otimes {\mathscr{F}}_3) \cong \mathrm{Hom}({\mathscr{F}}_2 \otimes {\mathscr{F}}_3^\vee,f_{23}^*p_{23*}(p_{X2}^*{\mathscr{E}}_{Z_2}^\vee \otimes p_{X3}^*{\mathscr{E}}_{Z_3})) \end{equation*} and note that $f_{23}^*p_{23*}(p_{X2}^*{\mathscr{E}}_{Z_2}^\vee \otimes p_{X3}^*{\mathscr{E}}_{Z_3})$ is a line bundle (again by Lemma~\ref{lemma:ps-ez}). The flatness over~$S$ of the cokernel ${\mathscr{O}}_{\mathscr{C}}$ of the morphism of~\eqref{eq:o-lines} is equivalent to the pointwise injectivity of the corresponding morphism ${\mathscr{F}}_2 \otimes {\mathscr{F}}_3^\vee \to f_{23}^*p_{23*}(p_{X2}^*{\mathscr{E}}_{Z_2}^\vee \otimes p_{X3}^*{\mathscr{E}}_{Z_3})$, i.e., to this map being an isomorphism. On the other hand, any line bundle on $S$ can be written as the tensor product of line bundles ${\mathscr{F}}_2 \otimes {\mathscr{F}}_3^\vee$ satisfying~\eqref{eq:f23-relation} in a unique way. This shows that the Hilbert scheme functor is isomorphic to the functor that associates to a scheme $S$ a pair of morphisms $f_2 \colon S \to Z_2$ and $f_3 \colon S \to Z_3$, hence is represented by $Z_2 \times Z_3$.

nodes.name: Flatness iff nonvanishing
nodes.statement: The flatness over $S$ of the cokernel ${\mathscr{O}}_{\mathscr{C}}$ of the morphism $(\mathrm{id}_X \times f_d)^*({\mathscr{E}}_{Z_d}^\vee) \otimes p_S^*({\mathscr{F}}_d) \to {\mathscr{O}}_{X \times S}$ is equivalent to the corresponding morphism ${\mathscr{F}}_d \to f_d^*p_{d*}{\mathscr{E}}_{Z_d}$ being nonzero for every closed point $s \in S$.
nodes.statement_short: Flatness iff nonvanishing

nodes.name: F_d(X) is the projective bundle
nodes.statement: Thus the Hilbert scheme functor $F_d(X)$ is isomorphic to the functor that associates to a scheme $S$ a morphism $f_d \colon S \to Z_d$ and a line subbundle in $f_d^*p_{d*}{\mathscr{E}}_{Z_d}$, hence is represented by the projective bundle ${\mathbb{P}}_{Z_d}(p_{d*}{\mathscr{E}}_{Z_d})$.
nodes.statement_short: F_d(X) is the projective bundle

nodes.name: Case d = 1 (lines)
nodes.statement: Now assume $d = 1$ and let ${\mathscr{C}} \subset X \times S$ be a flat family of lines. Decomposing ${\mathscr{O}}_{\mathscr{C}}$ with respect to~\eqref{eq:dbx-s} and using the argument of Theorem~\ref{theorem:moduli} together with the result of Lemma~\ref{lemma:oc-decomposition}$(ii)$, we conclude that there are morphisms $f_2 \colon S \to Z_2$ and $f_3 \colon S \to Z_3$, line bundles ${\mathscr{F}}_2$ and ${\mathscr{F}}_3$ on $S$, and an exact sequence \begin{equation} 0 \to (\mathrm{id}_X \times f_{2})^*({\mathscr{E}}_{Z_2}) \otimes p_S^*({\mathscr{F}}_2) \to (\mathrm{id}_X \times f_{3})^*({\mathscr{E}}_{Z_3}) \otimes p_S^*({\mathscr{F}}_3) \to {\mathscr{O}}_{\mathscr{C}} \to 0. \end{equation} Moreover, the pushforward to $S$ of this sequence gives (again by base change) an exact sequence \begin{equation*} 0 \to f_{2}^*(p_{2*}{\mathscr{E}}_{Z_2}) \otimes {\mathscr{F}}_2 \to f_{3}^*(p_{3*}{\mathscr{E}}_{Z_3}) \otimes {\mathscr{F}}_3 \to {\mathscr{O}}_S \to 0. \end{equation*} Since by Lemma~\ref{lemma:ps-ez} we know that $f_{d}^*(p_{d*}{\mathscr{E}}_{Z_d})$ is a vector bundle of rank $d$ on $S$, the comparison of determinants gives a relation \begin{equation} {\mathscr{F}}_3^3 \otimes {\mathscr{F}}_2^{-2} \cong f_{2}^*(\det(p_{2*}{\mathscr{E}}_{Z_2})) \otimes f_{3}^*(\det(p_{3*}{\mathscr{E}}_{Z_3})^{-1}). \end{equation} Denoting by $f_{23} \colon S \to Z_2 \times Z_3$ the map induced by $f_2$ and $f_3$, we deduce by adjunction and base change \begin{equation*} \mathrm{Hom}(f_{2}^*(p_{2*}{\mathscr{E}}_{Z_2}) \otimes {\mathscr{F}}_2, f_{3}^*(p_{3*}{\mathscr{E}}_{Z_3}) \otimes {\mathscr{F}}_3) \cong \mathrm{Hom}({\mathscr{F}}_2 \otimes {\mathscr{F}}_3^\vee,f_{23}^*p_{23*}(p_{X2}^*{\mathscr{E}}_{Z_2}^\vee \otimes p_{X3}^*{\mathscr{E}}_{Z_3})) \end{equation*} and note that $f_{23}^*p_{23*}(p_{X2}^*{\mathscr{E}}_{Z_2}^\vee \otimes p_{X3}^*{\mathscr{E}}_{Z_3})$ is a line bundle (again by Lemma~\ref{lemma:ps-ez}). The flatness over~$S$ of the cokernel ${\mathscr{O}}_{\mathscr{C}}$ of the morphism of~\eqref{eq:o-lines} is equivalent to the pointwise injectivity of the corresponding morphism ${\mathscr{F}}_2 \otimes {\mathscr{F}}_3^\vee \to f_{23}^*p_{23*}(p_{X2}^*{\mathscr{E}}_{Z_2}^\vee \otimes p_{X3}^*{\mathscr{E}}_{Z_3})$, i.e., to this map being an isomorphism. On the other hand, any line bundle on $S$ can be written as the tensor product of line bundles ${\mathscr{F}}_2 \otimes {\mathscr{F}}_3^\vee$ satisfying~\eqref{eq:f23-relation} in a unique way. This shows that the Hilbert scheme functor is isomorphic to the functor that associates to a scheme $S$ a pair of morphisms $f_2 \colon S \to Z_2$ and $f_3 \colon S \to Z_3$, hence is represented by $Z_2 \times Z_3$.
nodes.statement_short: Case d = 1 (lines)

nodes.name: Exact sequence for families of lines
nodes.statement: Decomposing ${\mathscr{O}}_{\mathscr{C}}$ with respect to~\eqref{eq:dbx-s} and using the argument of Theorem~\ref{theorem:moduli} together with the result of Lemma~\ref{lemma:oc-decomposition}$(ii)$, we conclude that there are morphisms $f_2 \colon S \to Z_2$ and $f_3 \colon S \to Z_3$, line bundles ${\mathscr{F}}_2$ and ${\mathscr{F}}_3$ on $S$, and an exact sequence \begin{equation} 0 \to (\mathrm{id}_X \times f_{2})^*({\mathscr{E}}_{Z_2}) \otimes p_S^*({\mathscr{F}}_2) \to (\mathrm{id}_X \times f_{3})^*({\mathscr{E}}_{Z_3}) \otimes p_S^*({\mathscr{F}}_3) \to {\mathscr{O}}_{\mathscr{C}} \to 0. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Exact sequence for families of lines

nodes.statement: 0 \to (\mathrm{id}_X \times f_{2})^*({\mathscr{E}}_{Z_2}) \otimes p_S^*({\mathscr{F}}_2) \to (\mathrm{id}_X \times f_{3})^*({\mathscr{E}}_{Z_3}) \otimes p_S^*({\mathscr{F}}_3) \to {\mathscr{O}}_{\mathscr{C}} \to 0.
nodes.name: Equation (38) o-lines
nodes.label: eq:o-lines

nodes.name: Push forward to S
nodes.statement: Moreover, the pushforward to $S$ of this sequence gives (again by base change) an exact sequence \begin{equation*} 0 \to f_{2}^*(p_{2*}{\mathscr{E}}_{Z_2}) \otimes {\mathscr{F}}_2 \to f_{3}^*(p_{3*}{\mathscr{E}}_{Z_3}) \otimes {\mathscr{F}}_3 \to {\mathscr{O}}_S \to 0. \end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: Push forward to S

nodes.name: Determinant relation
nodes.statement: Since by Lemma~\ref{lemma:ps-ez} we know that $f_{d}^*(p_{d*}{\mathscr{E}}_{Z_d})$ is a vector bundle of rank $d$ on $S$, the comparison of determinants gives a relation \begin{equation} {\mathscr{F}}_3^3 \otimes {\mathscr{F}}_2^{-2} \cong f_{2}^*(\det(p_{2*}{\mathscr{E}}_{Z_2})) \otimes f_{3}^*(\det(p_{3*}{\mathscr{E}}_{Z_3})^{-1}). \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Determinant relation

nodes.statement: {\mathscr{F}}_3^3 \otimes {\mathscr{F}}_2^{-2} \cong f_{2}^*(\det(p_{2*}{\mathscr{E}}_{Z_2})) \otimes f_{3}^*(\det(p_{3*}{\mathscr{E}}_{Z_3})^{-1}).
nodes.name: Equation (39) f23-relation
nodes.label: eq:f23-relation

nodes.name: Hom into a line bundle
nodes.statement: Denoting by $f_{23} \colon S \to Z_2 \times Z_3$ the map induced by $f_2$ and $f_3$, we deduce by adjunction and base change \begin{equation*} \mathrm{Hom}(f_{2}^*(p_{2*}{\mathscr{E}}_{Z_2}) \otimes {\mathscr{F}}_2, f_{3}^*(p_{3*}{\mathscr{E}}_{Z_3}) \otimes {\mathscr{F}}_3) \cong \mathrm{Hom}({\mathscr{F}}_2 \otimes {\mathscr{F}}_3^\vee,f_{23}^*p_{23*}(p_{X2}^*{\mathscr{E}}_{Z_2}^\vee \otimes p_{X3}^*{\mathscr{E}}_{Z_3})) \end{equation*} and note that $f_{23}^*p_{23*}(p_{X2}^*{\mathscr{E}}_{Z_2}^\vee \otimes p_{X3}^*{\mathscr{E}}_{Z_3})$ is a line bundle (again by Lemma~\ref{lemma:ps-ez}).
nodes.statement_short: Hom into a line bundle

nodes.name: Flatness iff isomorphism
nodes.statement: The flatness over~$S$ of the cokernel ${\mathscr{O}}_{\mathscr{C}}$ of the morphism of~\eqref{eq:o-lines} is equivalent to the pointwise injectivity of the corresponding morphism ${\mathscr{F}}_2 \otimes {\mathscr{F}}_3^\vee \to f_{23}^*p_{23*}(p_{X2}^*{\mathscr{E}}_{Z_2}^\vee \otimes p_{X3}^*{\mathscr{E}}_{Z_3})$, i.e., to this map being an isomorphism.
nodes.statement_short: Flatness iff isomorphism

nodes.name: Unique factorization of line bundles
nodes.statement: On the other hand, any line bundle on $S$ can be written as the tensor product of line bundles ${\mathscr{F}}_2 \otimes {\mathscr{F}}_3^\vee$ satisfying~\eqref{eq:f23-relation} in a unique way.
nodes.statement_short: Unique factorization of line bundles

nodes.name: F_1(X) = Z_2 x Z_3
nodes.statement: This shows that the Hilbert scheme functor is isomorphic to the functor that associates to a scheme $S$ a pair of morphisms $f_2 \colon S \to Z_2$ and $f_3 \colon S \to Z_3$, hence is represented by $Z_2 \times Z_3$.

With the same argument one can prove that $p_{2*}({\mathscr{E}}_{Z_2}^\vee \otimes \omega_X^{-1})$ is a rank-4 vector bundle on~$Z_2$ and that~$F_4(X) \cong {\mathbb{P}}_{Z_2}(p_{2*}({\mathscr{E}}_{Z_2}^\vee \otimes \omega_X^{-1}))$.
nodes.name: Hilbert scheme F_4(X)
nodes.label: remark:f4

nodes.statement: A family $f \colon {\mathscr{X}} \to S$ is a {\sf du Val family} of sextic del Pezzo surfaces, if $f$ is a flat projective morphism such that for every geometric point $s \in S$ the fiber ${\mathscr{X}}_s$ of ${\mathscr{X}}$ over $s$ is a sextic du Val del Pezzo surface (Definition~\ref{definition:dp6}), i.e., a normal integral surface with at worst du Val singularities such that $-K_{{\mathscr{X}}_s}$ is an ample Cartier divisor and $K_{{\mathscr{X}}_s}^2 = 6$.
nodes.name: Du Val family of sextic del Pezzo surfaces
nodes.statement_short: A flat projective morphism whose geometric fibers are sextic du Val del Pezzo surfaces.
differentia: for every geometric point $s \in S$ the fiber ${\mathscr{X}}_s$ of ${\mathscr{X}}$ over $s$ is a sextic du Val del Pezzo surface
nodes.label: definition:family-dp6

nodes.statement: Note also that by definition all fibers of $f \colon {\mathscr{X}} \to S$ are Gorenstein, hence the relative dualizing complex $\omega_{{\mathscr{X}}/S}^\bullet$ when restricted to any fiber of $f$ is an invertible sheaf, hence by Lemma~\ref{lemma:fiberwise} it is an invertible sheaf on the total space ${\mathscr{X}}$.
nodes.name: Relative dualizing complex of a du Val family is invertible

nodes.statement: If $f \colon {\mathscr{X}} \to S$ is a du Val family of sextic del Pezzo surfaces then for any base change $S' \to S$ the induced family $f' \colon {\mathscr{X}}' = {\mathscr{X}} \times_S S' \to S'$ is still a du Val family.
nodes.name: Du Val families are stable under base change
assumptions: $f \colon {\mathscr{X}} \to S$ is a du Val family of sextic del Pezzo surfaces
conclusions: is still a du Val family

nodes.statement: Assume $f \colon {\mathscr{X}} \to S$ is a du Val family of sextic del Pezzo surfaces. Then there is an~$S$-linear semiorthogonal decomposition \textup{(}compatible with any base change\textup{)} \begin{equation} {\mathbf{D}}({\mathscr{X}}) = \langle {\mathbf{D}}(S), {\mathbf{D}}({\mathscr{Z}}_2,\beta_{{\mathscr{Z}}_2}), {\mathbf{D}}({\mathscr{Z}}_3,\beta_{{\mathscr{Z}}_3}) \rangle, \end{equation} where ${\mathscr{Z}}_2 \to S$ and ${\mathscr{Z}}_3 \to S$ are finite flat morphisms of degree $3$ and $2$ respectively, $\beta_{{\mathscr{Z}}_2}$ and $\beta_{{\mathscr{Z}}_3}$ are Brauer classes of order $2$ and $3$ respectively on them, and the last two components are the twisted derived categories.
nodes.name: Semiorthogonal decomposition for families of sextic del Pezzo surfaces
nodes.statement_short: D(X) = <D(S), D(Z_2,beta_2), D(Z_3,beta_3)> for a du Val family, with Z_2, Z_3 finite flat of degrees 3, 2 and Brauer classes of order 2, 3.
assumptions: $f \colon {\mathscr{X}} \to S$ is a du Val family of sextic del Pezzo surfaces
conclusions: there is an~$S$-linear semiorthogonal decomposition
nodes.label: theorem:sod-dp6

nodes.statement: {\mathbf{D}}({\mathscr{X}}) = \langle {\mathbf{D}}(S), {\mathbf{D}}({\mathscr{Z}}_2,\beta_{{\mathscr{Z}}_2}), {\mathbf{D}}({\mathscr{Z}}_3,\beta_{{\mathscr{Z}}_3}) \rangle,
nodes.name: Equation (40) sod-dp6
nodes.label: eq:sod-dp6

nodes.statement: For $d \in \{2,3,4\}$ let ${\mathscr{M}}_d({\mathscr{X}}/S)$ denote the relative moduli stack of semistable sheaves on fibers of ${\mathscr{X}}$ over $S$ with Hilbert polynomial $h_d(t)$ defined in~\eqref{eq:hd}.
nodes.name: Relative moduli stack M_d(X/S)

nodes.statement: For $d \in \{2,3,4\}$ the stack ${\mathscr{M}}_d({\mathscr{X}}/S)$ is a ${\mathrm{G}_{\mathrm{m}}}$-gerbe over its coarse module space \begin{equation*} {\mathscr{Z}}_d({\mathscr{X}}/S) := ({\mathscr{M}}_d({\mathscr{X}}/S))_{\mathrm{coarse}} \end{equation*} with an obstruction given by a Brauer class $\beta_{{\mathscr{Z}}_d({\mathscr{X}}/S)}$ of order \begin{equation} \operatorname{ord} \beta_{{\mathscr{Z}}_d({\mathscr{X}}/S)} = \begin{cases} 2, & \text{if $d = 2$ or $d = 4$},\\ 3, & \text{if $d = 3$}. \end{cases} \end{equation} Moreover, there is an isomorphism of the coarse moduli spaces $\sigma_{2,4} \colon {\mathscr{Z}}_4({\mathscr{X}}/S) \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ } {\mathscr{Z}}_2({\mathscr{X}}/S)$ and an automorphism $\sigma_{3,3} \colon {\mathscr{Z}}_3({\mathscr{X}}/S) \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ } {\mathscr{Z}}_3({\mathscr{X}}/S)$, such that \begin{equation*} \beta_{{\mathscr{Z}}_4({\mathscr{X}}/S)} = \sigma_{2,4}^*(\beta_{{\mathscr{Z}}_2({\mathscr{X}}/S)}^{-1}) = \sigma_{2,4}^*(\beta_{{\mathscr{Z}}_2({\mathscr{X}}/S)}) \qquad\text{and}\qquad \beta_{{\mathscr{Z}}_3({\mathscr{X}}/S)} = \sigma_{3,3}^*(\beta_{{\mathscr{Z}}_3({\mathscr{X}}/S)}^{-1}). \end{equation*}
nodes.name: Relative moduli stacks are gerbes over Z_d
nodes.statement_short: M_d(X/S) is a G_m-gerbe over its coarse space Z_d with Brauer class of order 2 or 3; Z_4 = Z_2 and Z_3 has an involution.
conclusions: the stack ${\mathscr{M}}_d({\mathscr{X}}/S)$ is a ${\mathrm{G}_{\mathrm{m}}}$-gerbe over its coarse module space
nodes.label: proposition:md-zd

nodes.statement: \operatorname{ord} \beta_{{\mathscr{Z}}_d({\mathscr{X}}/S)} = \begin{cases} 2, & \text{if $d = 2$ or $d = 4$},\\ 3, & \text{if $d = 3$}. \end{cases}
nodes.name: Equation (41) brauer-order
nodes.label: eq:brauer-order

nodes.statement: By Lemma~\ref{lemma:hd-stable} all sheaves parameterized by the moduli stack ${\mathscr{M}}_d({\mathscr{X}}/S)$ are strictly stable. Therefore, by~\cite[Theorem~4.3.7]{huybrechts1997geometry}, the coarse moduli space ${{\mathscr{Z}}_d({\mathscr{X}}/S)}$ exists and there is a quasiuniversal family ${\mathscr{E}}_{{\mathscr{Z}}_d({\mathscr{X}}/S)}$ on the fiber product ${\mathscr{X}} \times_S {\mathscr{Z}}_d{({\mathscr{X}}/S)}$ which has a module structure over a sheaf of Azumaya algebras ${\mathscr{B}}_{{\mathscr{Z}}_d({\mathscr{X}}/S)}$ (defined up to a Morita equivalence) of order equal to the greatest common divisor of the values of the Hilbert polynomial $h_d(t)$ for $t \in {\mathbb{Z}}$. This means that ${\mathscr{M}}_d({\mathscr{X}}/S)$ is a ${\mathrm{G}_{\mathrm{m}}}$-gerbe over ${\mathscr{Z}}_d({\mathscr{X}}/S)$. Its obstruction class is given by the Brauer class $\beta_{{\mathscr{Z}}_d({\mathscr{X}}/S)}$ of the Azumaya algebra ${\mathscr{B}}_{{\mathscr{Z}}_d({\mathscr{X}}/S)}$, and a simple computation of the greatest common divisor of the values of the Hilbert polynomial $h_d(t)$ gives~\eqref{eq:brauer-order}. By Theorem~\ref{theorem:moduli} the sheaf ${\mathscr{E}}^\vee_{{\mathscr{Z}}_2({\mathscr{X}}/S)} \otimes \omega_{{\mathscr{X}}/S}^{-1}$ on ${\mathscr{X}} \times_S {\mathscr{Z}}_2({\mathscr{X}}/S)$ provides a family of stable sheaves with Hilbert polynomial $h_4(t)$ and the sheaf ${\mathscr{E}}^\vee_{{\mathscr{Z}}_4({\mathscr{X}}/S)} \otimes \omega_{{\mathscr{X}}/S}^{-1}$ on ${\mathscr{X}} \times_S {\mathscr{Z}}_4({\mathscr{X}}/S)$ provides a family of stable sheaves with Hilbert polynomial $h_2(t)$. Therefore, the moduli stacks ${\mathscr{M}}_2({\mathscr{X}}/S)$ and ${\mathscr{M}}_4({\mathscr{X}}/S)$ are isomorphic. Denoting by $\sigma_{2,4}$ the induced isomorphism of the coarse moduli spaces, we conclude that the family $\sigma_{2,4}^*({\mathscr{E}}^\vee_{{\mathscr{Z}}_2({\mathscr{X}}/S)} \otimes \omega_{{\mathscr{X}}/S}^{-1})$ is a quasiuniversal family on ${\mathscr{X}} \times_S {\mathscr{Z}}_4({\mathscr{X}}/S)$. It follows that the pullback of the opposite Azumaya algebra ${\mathscr{B}}_{{\mathscr{Z}}_2({\mathscr{X}}/s)}$ to ${\mathscr{Z}}_4({\mathscr{X}}/S)$ is Morita-equivalent to the Azumaya algebra ${\mathscr{B}}_{{\mathscr{Z}}_4({\mathscr{X}}/S)}$, hence $\beta_{{\mathscr{Z}}_4({\mathscr{X}}/S)} = \sigma_{2,4}^*(\beta_{{\mathscr{Z}}_2({\mathscr{X}}/S)}^{-1})$. Since by~\eqref{eq:brauer-order} the order of $\beta_{{\mathscr{Z}}_2({\mathscr{X}}/S)}$ is~2, this can be also written as~$\sigma_{2,4}^*(\beta_{{\mathscr{Z}}_2({\mathscr{X}}/S)}^{-1})$. The second isomorphism $\sigma_{3,3}$ is constructed in the same way, and with its construction we also get an isomorphism of quasiuniversal families and an equality of Brauer classes.
nodes.statement_short: Coarse moduli via Huybrechts-Lehn; Brauer order from gcd of Hilbert polynomial values; dual families identify M_2 and M_4.
nodes.name: Proof of Relative moduli stacks are gerbes over Z_d
All sheaves are stable
nodes.statement: By Lemma~\ref{lemma:hd-stable} all sheaves parameterized by the moduli stack ${\mathscr{M}}_d({\mathscr{X}}/S)$ are strictly stable.
nodes.statement_short: All sheaves are stable

nodes.name: Coarse space, quasiuniversal family, gerbe and Brauer order
nodes.statement: Therefore, by~\cite[Theorem~4.3.7]{huybrechts1997geometry}, the coarse moduli space ${{\mathscr{Z}}_d({\mathscr{X}}/S)}$ exists and there is a quasiuniversal family ${\mathscr{E}}_{{\mathscr{Z}}_d({\mathscr{X}}/S)}$ on the fiber product ${\mathscr{X}} \times_S {\mathscr{Z}}_d{({\mathscr{X}}/S)}$ which has a module structure over a sheaf of Azumaya algebras ${\mathscr{B}}_{{\mathscr{Z}}_d({\mathscr{X}}/S)}$ (defined up to a Morita equivalence) of order equal to the greatest common divisor of the values of the Hilbert polynomial $h_d(t)$ for $t \in {\mathbb{Z}}$. This means that ${\mathscr{M}}_d({\mathscr{X}}/S)$ is a ${\mathrm{G}_{\mathrm{m}}}$-gerbe over ${\mathscr{Z}}_d({\mathscr{X}}/S)$. Its obstruction class is given by the Brauer class $\beta_{{\mathscr{Z}}_d({\mathscr{X}}/S)}$ of the Azumaya algebra ${\mathscr{B}}_{{\mathscr{Z}}_d({\mathscr{X}}/S)}$, and a simple computation of the greatest common divisor of the values of the Hilbert polynomial $h_d(t)$ gives~\eqref{eq:brauer-order}.
nodes.statement_short: Coarse space, quasiuniversal family, gerbe and Brauer order

nodes.name: Dual families identify M_2 and M_4
nodes.statement: By Theorem~\ref{theorem:moduli} the sheaf ${\mathscr{E}}^\vee_{{\mathscr{Z}}_2({\mathscr{X}}/S)} \otimes \omega_{{\mathscr{X}}/S}^{-1}$ on ${\mathscr{X}} \times_S {\mathscr{Z}}_2({\mathscr{X}}/S)$ provides a family of stable sheaves with Hilbert polynomial $h_4(t)$ and the sheaf ${\mathscr{E}}^\vee_{{\mathscr{Z}}_4({\mathscr{X}}/S)} \otimes \omega_{{\mathscr{X}}/S}^{-1}$ on ${\mathscr{X}} \times_S {\mathscr{Z}}_4({\mathscr{X}}/S)$ provides a family of stable sheaves with Hilbert polynomial $h_2(t)$. Therefore, the moduli stacks ${\mathscr{M}}_2({\mathscr{X}}/S)$ and ${\mathscr{M}}_4({\mathscr{X}}/S)$ are isomorphic.
nodes.statement_short: Dual families identify M_2 and M_4

nodes.name: Relation of Brauer classes
nodes.statement: Denoting by $\sigma_{2,4}$ the induced isomorphism of the coarse moduli spaces, we conclude that the family $\sigma_{2,4}^*({\mathscr{E}}^\vee_{{\mathscr{Z}}_2({\mathscr{X}}/S)} \otimes \omega_{{\mathscr{X}}/S}^{-1})$ is a quasiuniversal family on ${\mathscr{X}} \times_S {\mathscr{Z}}_4({\mathscr{X}}/S)$. It follows that the pullback of the opposite Azumaya algebra ${\mathscr{B}}_{{\mathscr{Z}}_2({\mathscr{X}}/s)}$ to ${\mathscr{Z}}_4({\mathscr{X}}/S)$ is Morita-equivalent to the Azumaya algebra ${\mathscr{B}}_{{\mathscr{Z}}_4({\mathscr{X}}/S)}$, hence $\beta_{{\mathscr{Z}}_4({\mathscr{X}}/S)} = \sigma_{2,4}^*(\beta_{{\mathscr{Z}}_2({\mathscr{X}}/S)}^{-1})$. Since by~\eqref{eq:brauer-order} the order of $\beta_{{\mathscr{Z}}_2({\mathscr{X}}/S)}$ is~2, this can be also written as~$\sigma_{2,4}^*(\beta_{{\mathscr{Z}}_2({\mathscr{X}}/S)}^{-1})$.
nodes.statement_short: Relation of Brauer classes

nodes.name: Same for sigma_{3,3}
nodes.statement: The second isomorphism $\sigma_{3,3}$ is constructed in the same way, and with its construction we also get an isomorphism of quasiuniversal families and an equality of Brauer classes.
nodes.statement_short: Same for sigma_{3,3}

nodes.statement: We denote by \begin{equation*} f_d \colon {\mathscr{Z}}_d \to S \end{equation*} the natural projection.
nodes.name: Projection f_d: Z_d -> S

nodes.statement: We replace the Azumaya algebra ${\mathscr{B}}_{{\mathscr{Z}}_d}$ by its Brauer class $\beta_{{\mathscr{Z}}_d} \in \mathrm{Br}({\mathscr{Z}}_d)$ and consider the quasiuniversal family as a~$\beta^{-1}_{{\mathscr{Z}}_d}$-twisted family of sheaves on ${\mathscr{X}} \times_S {\mathscr{Z}}_d$: \begin{equation*} {\mathscr{E}}_{{\mathscr{Z}}_d} \in \mathrm{coh}({\mathscr{X}} \times_S {\mathscr{Z}}_d, \beta^{-1}_{{\mathscr{Z}}_d}).
nodes.name: Twisted universal family E_{Z_d}

nodes.statement: Let $\phi \colon S' \to S$ be a base change and denote ${\mathscr{X}}' := {\mathscr{X}} \times_S S'$. We have \begin{equation} {\mathscr{M}}_d({\mathscr{X}}'/S') \cong {\mathscr{M}}_d({\mathscr{X}}/S) \times_S S' \qquad\text{and}\qquad {\mathscr{Z}}_d({\mathscr{X}}'/S') \cong {\mathscr{Z}}_d({\mathscr{X}}/S) \times_S S'. \end{equation} Moreover, isomorphisms~\eqref{eq:md-zd-base-change} are compatible with the universal families, i.e., \begin{equation} \beta_{{\mathscr{Z}}'_d} = \phi_{{\mathscr{Z}}_d}^*(\beta_{{\mathscr{Z}}_d}) \qquad\text{and}\qquad {\mathscr{E}}_{{\mathscr{Z}}'_d} \cong \phi_{{\mathscr{X}} \times_S {\mathscr{Z}}_d}^*{\mathscr{E}}_{{\mathscr{Z}}_d}. \end{equation} where we set ${\mathscr{Z}}'_d := {\mathscr{Z}}_d({\mathscr{X}}'/S')$ and denote the morphisms induced by the base change by $\phi_{\mathscr{X}} \colon {\mathscr{X}}' \to {\mathscr{X}}$, $\phi_{{\mathscr{Z}}_d} \colon {\mathscr{Z}}'_d \to {\mathscr{Z}}_d$, and $\phi_{{\mathscr{X}} \times_S {\mathscr{Z}}_d} \colon {\mathscr{X}}' \times_{S'} {\mathscr{Z}}'_d \to {\mathscr{X}} \times_S {\mathscr{Z}}_d$, respectively.
nodes.name: Base change for M_d and Z_d
assumptions: $\phi \colon S' \to S$ be a base change
conclusions: isomorphisms~\eqref{eq:md-zd-base-change} are compatible with the universal families
nodes.label: lemma:md-zd-base-change

nodes.statement: {\mathscr{M}}_d({\mathscr{X}}'/S') \cong {\mathscr{M}}_d({\mathscr{X}}/S) \times_S S' \qquad\text{and}\qquad {\mathscr{Z}}_d({\mathscr{X}}'/S') \cong {\mathscr{Z}}_d({\mathscr{X}}/S) \times_S S'.
nodes.name: Equation (42) md-zd-base-change
nodes.label: eq:md-zd-base-change

nodes.statement: \beta_{{\mathscr{Z}}'_d} = \phi_{{\mathscr{Z}}_d}^*(\beta_{{\mathscr{Z}}_d}) \qquad\text{and}\qquad {\mathscr{E}}_{{\mathscr{Z}}'_d} \cong \phi_{{\mathscr{X}} \times_S {\mathscr{Z}}_d}^*{\mathscr{E}}_{{\mathscr{Z}}_d}.
nodes.name: Equation (43) ced-base-change
nodes.label: eq:ced-base-change

nodes.statement: The first isomorphism in~\eqref{eq:md-zd-base-change} is clear from the definition of a relative moduli space, and the second follows from the GIT construction of the coarse moduli space. Since the pullback of a universal family is a $\phi_{{\mathscr{Z}}_d}^*(\beta_{{\mathscr{Z}}_d})$-twisted family of stable sheaves on fibers of ${\mathscr{X}}'$ over $S'$, the equality of the Brauer classes and the isomorphism of universal families follow.
nodes.statement_short: Moduli definition and GIT give base change; pullback of universal family.
nodes.name: Proof of Base change for M_d and Z_d

nodes.statement: For any geometric point $s \in S$ there are isomorphisms \begin{equation} {\mathscr{M}}_d({\mathscr{X}}/S)_s \cong {\mathscr{M}}_d(X), \qquad {\mathscr{Z}}_d({\mathscr{X}}/S)_s \cong Z_d \qquad\text{and}\qquad i_{Z_d}^*({\mathscr{E}}_{{\mathscr{Z}}_d}) \cong {\mathscr{E}}_{Z_d}, \end{equation} where $X = {\mathscr{X}}_s$ is the fiber of ${\mathscr{X}}$ over $s$ and $i_{Z_d} \colon Z_d \cong {\mathscr{Z}}_d({\mathscr{X}}/S)_s \hookrightarrow {\mathscr{Z}}_d({\mathscr{X}}/S)$ is the natural embedding.
nodes.name: Fibers of Z_d over geometric points
assumptions: For any geometric point $s \in S$
conclusions: there are isomorphisms
nodes.label: corollary:S-s

nodes.statement: {\mathscr{M}}_d({\mathscr{X}}/S)_s \cong {\mathscr{M}}_d(X), \qquad {\mathscr{Z}}_d({\mathscr{X}}/S)_s \cong Z_d \qquad\text{and}\qquad i_{Z_d}^*({\mathscr{E}}_{{\mathscr{Z}}_d}) \cong {\mathscr{E}}_{Z_d},
nodes.name: Equation (44) m-z-e-s
nodes.label: eq:m-z-e-s

nodes.statement: The maps $f_2 \colon {\mathscr{Z}}_2 \to S$ and $f_3 \colon {\mathscr{Z}}_3 \to S$ are finite flat maps of degree $3$ and $2$ respectively. The relative dualizing complexes $\omega_{{\mathscr{Z}}_2/S}^\bullet$ and $\omega_{{\mathscr{Z}}_3/S}^\bullet$ are line bundles.
nodes.name: Z_2 and Z_3 are finite flat over S
conclusions: The maps $f_2 \colon {\mathscr{Z}}_2 \to S$ and $f_3 \colon {\mathscr{Z}}_3 \to S$ are finite flat maps of degree $3$ and $2$ respectively
nodes.label: lemma:zd-flat

nodes.statement: Since flatness can be verified on an \'etale covering (note that formation of schemes ${\mathscr{Z}}_d$ is compatible with base changes by~\eqref{eq:md-zd-base-change}) and the moduli stack of du Val sextic del Pezzo surfaces is smooth by Theorem~\ref{theorem:moduli-stack-dp6}, we may assume that $S$ is smooth over ${\mathsf{k}}$, hence reduced. Since ${\mathscr{Z}}_d$ is proper over $S$, it is enough to show that the (scheme-theoretic) fiber of ${\mathscr{Z}}_d$ over any geometric point ${{s}} \in S$ is zero-dimensional of length~$6/d$. But as it was mentioned in Corollary~\ref{corollary:S-s}, the fiber $({\mathscr{Z}}_d)_s$ is identified with the zero-dimensional scheme~$Z_d$ associated with the surface $X = {\mathscr{X}}_s$, and hence its length is indeed~$6/d$, see Corollary~\ref{corollary:dbx-z2-z3}. Since $f_d$ is flat, to check that the relative dualizing complex is a line bundle, it is enough to check that each fiber of $f_d$ is a Gorenstein scheme, which holds true by~\eqref{eq:m-z-e-s} and Corollary~\ref{corollary:dbx-z2-z3}.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to smooth base via smoothness of the moduli stack; fibers are Z_d of length 6/d and Gorenstein.

The kernel~${\mathscr{E}}_{{\mathscr{Z}}_d}^\vee \otimes p_d^*\omega_{{\mathscr{Z}}_d/S}$ of this functor is compativle with base changes, i.e., if $\phi \colon S' \to S$ is a base change, then \begin{equation*} \phi_{{\mathscr{X}} \times_S {\mathscr{Z}}_d}^*({\mathscr{E}}_{{\mathscr{Z}}_d}^\vee \otimes p_d^*\omega_{{\mathscr{Z}}_d/S}) \cong {\mathscr{E}}_{{\mathscr{Z}}'_d}^\vee \otimes p_d^{\prime*}\omega_{{\mathscr{Z}}'_d/S'}. \end{equation*}

nodes.statement: For the first part it is enough to show that \begin{equation} \mathrm{R}\mathscr{H}\mathit{om}({\mathscr{E}}_{{\mathscr{Z}}_d},p^!{\mathscr{G}}) \cong {\mathscr{E}}_{{\mathscr{Z}}_d}^\vee \otimes p_d^*\omega_{{\mathscr{Z}}_d/S} \otimes p^*({\mathscr{G}}). \end{equation} For this we use an argument of Neeman from~\cite[Theorem~5.4]{neeman1996grothendieck}. First, the functor in the right hand side of~\eqref{eq:isomorphism-functors} commutes with arbitrary direct sums since the pullback and the tensor product functors do. The functor in the left hand side is right adjoint to the functor~$p_*({\mathscr{E}}_{{\mathscr{Z}}_d} \otimes (-))$. The latter functor preserves perfectness by an argument analogous to that of Lemma~\ref{lemma:phi-d-shriek}, hence the former commutes with direct sums by~\cite[Theorem~5.1]{neeman1996grothendieck}. Further, if ${\mathscr{G}}$ is a perfect complex, then $p^!({\mathscr{G}}) \cong p^*({\mathscr{G}}) \otimes p_d^*\omega^\bullet_{{\mathscr{Z}}_d/S}$. By Lemma~\ref{lemma:zd-flat} the dualizing complex~$\omega^\bullet_{{\mathscr{Z}}_d/S}$ is a line bundle $\omega_{{\mathscr{Z}}_d/S}$, hence $p^!({\mathscr{G}})$ is a perfect complex, and~\eqref{eq:isomorphism-functors} in this case follows. Now the Neeman's trick comes. There is a natural transformation from the functor in the right hand side of~\eqref{eq:isomorphism-functors} to the functor in the left hand side. The subcategory of objects on which this transformation is an isomorphism is a triangulated subcategory of the unbounded derived category of ${\mathscr{X}}$ which contains all perfect complexes and is closed under arbitrary direct sums, hence is the whole category. This proves~\eqref{eq:isomorphism-functors} for all ${\mathscr{G}}$. The fact that ${\mathscr{E}}_{{\mathscr{Z}}_d}^\vee$ is a sheaf flat over ${\mathscr{Z}}_d$ follows from the isomorphisms in the proof of Proposition~\ref{proposition:md-zd} since $\omega_{{\mathscr{X}}/S}$ is a line bundle. Using Lemma~\ref{lemma:md-zd-base-change} we deduce the required base change isomorphism.
nodes.statement_short: Neeman's trick: both sides commute with direct sums and agree on perfect complexes.

It remains to note that both $\Phi_d$ and $\Phi_d^!$ are Fourier--Mukai functors (the first by definition~\eqref{eq:phid-definition} and the second by Lemma~\ref{lemma:phid-shriek-other}).
nodes.statement_short: Kuznetsov's base change lemma for Fourier-Mukai functors.
nodes.name: Proof of Base change compatibility of Phi_d and Phi_d^!

nodes.statement: Take $d_1,d_2 \in \{1,2,3\}$ and consider the diagram \begin{equation*} \xymatrix{ & {\mathscr{Z}}_{d_1} \times_S {\mathscr{X}} \times_S {\mathscr{Z}}_{d_2} \ar[dl]_{\mathrm{pr}_{1,2}} \ar[d]^{\mathrm{pr}_{1,3}} \ar[dr]^{\mathrm{pr}_{2,3}} \\ {\mathscr{Z}}_{d_1} \times_S {\mathscr{X}} & {\mathscr{Z}}_{d_1} \times_S {\mathscr{Z}}_{d_2} & {\mathscr{X}} \times_S {\mathscr{Z}}_{d_2} } \end{equation*} A standard computation shows that the composition of functors $\Phi_{d_2}^! \circ \Phi_{d_1}$ is a Fourier--Mukai functor given by the object \begin{equation} \mathrm{pr}_{1,3*}(\mathrm{pr}_{2,3}^*({\mathscr{E}}_{{\mathscr{Z}}_{d_2}}^\vee \otimes p_{d_2}^*\omega_{{\mathscr{Z}}_{d_2}/S}) \otimes \mathrm{pr}_{1,2}^*({\mathscr{E}}_{{\mathscr{Z}}_{d_1}})) \in {\mathbf{D}}({\mathscr{Z}}_{d_1} \times_S {\mathscr{Z}}_{d_2}, \beta_{{\mathscr{Z}}_{d_1}}^{-1} \boxtimes \beta_{{\mathscr{Z}}_{d_2}}). \end{equation} Let us prove that $\Phi_d$ is fully faithful for each $d \in \{1,2,3\}$. For this it is enough to check that the object~\eqref{eq:convolution} in case $d_1 = d_2 = d$ is isomorphic (via the unit of adjunction morphism) to the structure sheaf of the diagonal. Since the unit of the adjunction is induced by a morphism of kernels \cite{anno2012adjunction}, by Lemma~\ref{lemma:fiberwise} it is enough to check that for any geometric point $s \in S$ we have \begin{equation} i_{Z_d \times Z_d}^*(\mathrm{pr}_{1,3*}(\mathrm{pr}_{2,3}^*({\mathscr{E}}_{{\mathscr{Z}}_{d}}^\vee \otimes p_{d}^*\omega_{{\mathscr{Z}}_{d}/S}) \otimes \mathrm{pr}_{1,2}^*({\mathscr{E}}_{{\mathscr{Z}}_{d}}))) \cong \delta_*{\mathscr{O}}_{Z_d} \in {\mathbf{D}}(Z_d \times Z_d) \end{equation} where $i_{Z_d \times Z_d} \colon Z_d \times Z_d \to {\mathscr{Z}}_d \times_S {\mathscr{Z}}_d$ is the natural embedding and $\delta \colon Z_d \to Z_d \times Z_d$ is the diagonal. Using base change and isomorphisms of Lemma~\ref{lemma:md-zd-base-change} and Lemma~\ref{lemma:phid-shriek-other}, we can rewrite the left hand side of~\eqref{eq:isomorphism-diagonal} as the Fourier--Mukai kernel of the functor \begin{equation*} {\mathbf{D}}(Z_d) \xrightarrow{\ \Phi_{{\mathscr{E}}_{Z_d}}\ } {\mathbf{D}}(X) \xrightarrow{\ \Phi_{{\mathscr{E}}_{Z_d}}^!\ } {\mathbf{D}}(Z_d), \end{equation*} where the functor $\Phi_{{\mathscr{E}}_{Z_d}}$ is identified in Proposition~\ref{proposition:fm-zd} with the equivalence ${\mathbf{D}}(Z_d) \cong {\mathcal{A}}_d \subset {\mathbf{D}}(X)$, and~$\Phi_{{\mathscr{E}}_{Z_d}}^!$ is its right adjoint. This composition is isomorphic to the identity, since the functor $\Phi_{{\mathscr{E}}_{Z_d}}$ is fully faithful, hence we have~\eqref{eq:isomorphism-diagonal}. Therefore, the functor $\Phi_d$ is fully faithful. Next, let us prove that the subcategories $\Phi_d({\mathbf{D}}({\mathscr{Z}}_d,\beta_{{\mathscr{Z}}_d})) \subset {\mathbf{D}}({\mathscr{X}})$ for $1 \le d \le 3$ are semiorthogonal. For this it is enough to check that the object~\eqref{eq:convolution} in case $d_1 < d_2$ is zero. Again, using Lemma~\ref{lemma:fiberwise} and base change isomorphisms of Lemma~\ref{lemma:md-zd-base-change} and Lemma~\ref{lemma:phid-shriek-other} we reduce to the case of $S = \mathrm{Spec}({\mathsf{k}})$ with algebraically closed ${\mathsf{k}}$. In the latter case, the required vanishing follows from semiorthogonality of the subcategories $\Phi_{{\mathscr{E}}_{Z_{d_i}}}({\mathbf{D}}(Z_{d_i})) = {\mathcal{A}}_{d_i}$ in ${\mathbf{D}}(X)$. Finally, let us prove that the subcategories $\Phi_d({\mathbf{D}}({\mathscr{Z}}_d,\beta_{{\mathscr{Z}}_d})) \subset {\mathbf{D}}({\mathscr{X}})$ for $1 \le d \le 3$ generate ${\mathbf{D}}({\mathscr{X}})$. Take any ${\mathscr{G}} \in {\mathbf{D}}({\mathscr{X}})$ and set \begin{equation*} {\mathscr{G}}_2 := \mathrm{Cone}(\Phi_3\Phi_3^!{\mathscr{G}} \to {\mathscr{G}}), \qquad {\mathscr{G}}_1 := \mathrm{Cone}(\Phi_2\Phi_2^!{\mathscr{G}}_2 \to {\mathscr{G}}_2), \qquad\text{and}\qquad {\mathscr{G}}_0 := \mathrm{Cone}(\Phi_1\Phi_1^!{\mathscr{G}}_1 \to {\mathscr{G}}_1). \end{equation*} From full faithfulness and semiorthogonality it easily follows that $\Phi_1^!({\mathscr{G}}_0) = \Phi_2^!({\mathscr{G}}_0) = \Phi_3^!({\mathscr{G}}_0) = 0$. Then Lemma~\ref{lemma:phid-linear} implies that for any geometric point $s \in S$ setting ${\mathscr{G}}_{0s} = i_{X}^*({\mathscr{G}}_0) \in {\mathbf{D}}(X)$ to be the restriction of ${\mathscr{G}}_0$ to the fiber $X = {\mathscr{X}}_s$, we have $\Phi_d^!({\mathscr{G}}_{0s}) = 0$ for all $d$. By semiorthogonal decomposition~\eqref{eq:dbx-dz} this means that ${\mathscr{G}}_{0s} = 0$. Hence by Lemma~\ref{lemma:fiberwise}$(i)$ we have ${\mathscr{G}}_0 = 0$. Thus we have a chain of morphisms \begin{equation*} {\mathscr{G}} =: {\mathscr{G}}_3 \to {\mathscr{G}}_2 \to {\mathscr{G}}_1 \to {\mathscr{G}}_0 = 0 \end{equation*} with $\mathrm{Cone}({\mathscr{G}}_{d} \to {\mathscr{G}}_{d-1}) \in \Phi_d({\mathbf{D}}({\mathscr{Z}}_d,\beta_{{\mathscr{Z}}_d}))$, which proves the required semiorthogonal decomposition. This semiorthogonal decomposition is $S$-linear since by Lemma~\ref{lemma:phi-d-shriek} its embedding functors~$\Phi_d$ are $S$-linear, and its compatibility with base changes follows from~\cite[Theorem~6.4]{kuznetsov2011base} together with Lemma~\ref{lemma:phid-linear} and Lemma~\ref{lemma:md-zd-base-change}.

Since the unit of the adjunction is induced by a morphism of kernels \cite{anno2012adjunction}, by Lemma~\ref{lemma:fiberwise} it is enough to check that for any geometric point $s \in S$ we have \begin{equation} i_{Z_d \times Z_d}^*(\mathrm{pr}_{1,3*}(\mathrm{pr}_{2,3}^*({\mathscr{E}}_{{\mathscr{Z}}_{d}}^\vee \otimes p_{d}^*\omega_{{\mathscr{Z}}_{d}/S}) \otimes \mathrm{pr}_{1,2}^*({\mathscr{E}}_{{\mathscr{Z}}_{d}}))) \cong \delta_*{\mathscr{O}}_{Z_d} \in {\mathbf{D}}(Z_d \times Z_d) \end{equation} where $i_{Z_d \times Z_d} \colon Z_d \times Z_d \to {\mathscr{Z}}_d \times_S {\mathscr{Z}}_d$ is the natural embedding and $\delta \colon Z_d \to Z_d \times Z_d$ is the diagonal. Using base change and isomorphisms of Lemma~\ref{lemma:md-zd-base-change} and Lemma~\ref{lemma:phid-shriek-other}, we can rewrite the left hand side of~\eqref{eq:isomorphism-diagonal} as the Fourier--Mukai kernel of the functor \begin{equation*} {\mathbf{D}}(Z_d) \xrightarrow{\ \Phi_{{\mathscr{E}}_{Z_d}}\ } {\mathbf{D}}(X) \xrightarrow{\ \Phi_{{\mathscr{E}}_{Z_d}}^!\ } {\mathbf{D}}(Z_d), \end{equation*} where the functor $\Phi_{{\mathscr{E}}_{Z_d}}$ is identified in Proposition~\ref{proposition:fm-zd} with the equivalence ${\mathbf{D}}(Z_d) \cong {\mathcal{A}}_d \subset {\mathbf{D}}(X)$, and~$\Phi_{{\mathscr{E}}_{Z_d}}^!$ is its right adjoint. This composition is isomorphic to the identity, since the functor $\Phi_{{\mathscr{E}}_{Z_d}}$ is fully faithful, hence we have~\eqref{eq:isomorphism-diagonal}. Therefore, the functor $\Phi_d$ is fully faithful.
nodes.statement_short: Full faithfulness

nodes.name: Reduce to kernel being the diagonal
nodes.statement: For this it is enough to check that the object~\eqref{eq:convolution} in case $d_1 = d_2 = d$ is isomorphic (via the unit of adjunction morphism) to the structure sheaf of the diagonal.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to kernel being the diagonal

nodes.name: Check on geometric fibers
nodes.statement: Since the unit of the adjunction is induced by a morphism of kernels \cite{anno2012adjunction}, by Lemma~\ref{lemma:fiberwise} it is enough to check that for any geometric point $s \in S$ we have \begin{equation} i_{Z_d \times Z_d}^*(\mathrm{pr}_{1,3*}(\mathrm{pr}_{2,3}^*({\mathscr{E}}_{{\mathscr{Z}}_{d}}^\vee \otimes p_{d}^*\omega_{{\mathscr{Z}}_{d}/S}) \otimes \mathrm{pr}_{1,2}^*({\mathscr{E}}_{{\mathscr{Z}}_{d}}))) \cong \delta_*{\mathscr{O}}_{Z_d} \in {\mathbf{D}}(Z_d \times Z_d) \end{equation} where $i_{Z_d \times Z_d} \colon Z_d \times Z_d \to {\mathscr{Z}}_d \times_S {\mathscr{Z}}_d$ is the natural embedding and $\delta \colon Z_d \to Z_d \times Z_d$ is the diagonal.
nodes.statement_short: Check on geometric fibers

nodes.statement: i_{Z_d \times Z_d}^*(\mathrm{pr}_{1,3*}(\mathrm{pr}_{2,3}^*({\mathscr{E}}_{{\mathscr{Z}}_{d}}^\vee \otimes p_{d}^*\omega_{{\mathscr{Z}}_{d}/S}) \otimes \mathrm{pr}_{1,2}^*({\mathscr{E}}_{{\mathscr{Z}}_{d}}))) \cong \delta_*{\mathscr{O}}_{Z_d} \in {\mathbf{D}}(Z_d \times Z_d)
nodes.name: Equation (51) isomorphism-diagonal
nodes.label: eq:isomorphism-diagonal

nodes.name: Fiber is the kernel of Phi^! Phi on X
nodes.statement: Using base change and isomorphisms of Lemma~\ref{lemma:md-zd-base-change} and Lemma~\ref{lemma:phid-shriek-other}, we can rewrite the left hand side of~\eqref{eq:isomorphism-diagonal} as the Fourier--Mukai kernel of the functor \begin{equation*} {\mathbf{D}}(Z_d) \xrightarrow{\ \Phi_{{\mathscr{E}}_{Z_d}}\ } {\mathbf{D}}(X) \xrightarrow{\ \Phi_{{\mathscr{E}}_{Z_d}}^!\ } {\mathbf{D}}(Z_d), \end{equation*} where the functor $\Phi_{{\mathscr{E}}_{Z_d}}$ is identified in Proposition~\ref{proposition:fm-zd} with the equivalence ${\mathbf{D}}(Z_d) \cong {\mathcal{A}}_d \subset {\mathbf{D}}(X)$, and~$\Phi_{{\mathscr{E}}_{Z_d}}^!$ is its right adjoint.
nodes.statement_short: Fiber is the kernel of Phi^! Phi on X

nodes.name: Identity since Phi_{E_{Z_d}} is fully faithful
nodes.statement: This composition is isomorphic to the identity, since the functor $\Phi_{{\mathscr{E}}_{Z_d}}$ is fully faithful, hence we have~\eqref{eq:isomorphism-diagonal}. Therefore, the functor $\Phi_d$ is fully faithful.
nodes.statement_short: Identity since Phi_{E_{Z_d}} is fully faithful

nodes.name: Semiorthogonality reduces to vanishing of the kernel
nodes.statement: Next, let us prove that the subcategories $\Phi_d({\mathbf{D}}({\mathscr{Z}}_d,\beta_{{\mathscr{Z}}_d})) \subset {\mathbf{D}}({\mathscr{X}})$ for $1 \le d \le 3$ are semiorthogonal. For this it is enough to check that the object~\eqref{eq:convolution} in case $d_1 < d_2$ is zero.
nodes.statement_short: Semiorthogonality reduces to vanishing of the kernel

nodes.name: Reduce to a single surface
nodes.statement: Again, using Lemma~\ref{lemma:fiberwise} and base change isomorphisms of Lemma~\ref{lemma:md-zd-base-change} and Lemma~\ref{lemma:phid-shriek-other} we reduce to the case of $S = \mathrm{Spec}({\mathsf{k}})$ with algebraically closed ${\mathsf{k}}$. In the latter case, the required vanishing follows from semiorthogonality of the subcategories $\Phi_{{\mathscr{E}}_{Z_{d_i}}}({\mathbf{D}}(Z_{d_i})) = {\mathcal{A}}_{d_i}$ in ${\mathbf{D}}(X)$.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to a single surface

nodes.name: Generation: successive cones G_2, G_1, G_0
nodes.statement: Finally, let us prove that the subcategories $\Phi_d({\mathbf{D}}({\mathscr{Z}}_d,\beta_{{\mathscr{Z}}_d})) \subset {\mathbf{D}}({\mathscr{X}})$ for $1 \le d \le 3$ generate ${\mathbf{D}}({\mathscr{X}})$. Take any ${\mathscr{G}} \in {\mathbf{D}}({\mathscr{X}})$ and set \begin{equation*} {\mathscr{G}}_2 := \mathrm{Cone}(\Phi_3\Phi_3^!{\mathscr{G}} \to {\mathscr{G}}), \qquad {\mathscr{G}}_1 := \mathrm{Cone}(\Phi_2\Phi_2^!{\mathscr{G}}_2 \to {\mathscr{G}}_2), \qquad\text{and}\qquad {\mathscr{G}}_0 := \mathrm{Cone}(\Phi_1\Phi_1^!{\mathscr{G}}_1 \to {\mathscr{G}}_1). \end{equation*} From full faithfulness and semiorthogonality it easily follows that $\Phi_1^!({\mathscr{G}}_0) = \Phi_2^!({\mathscr{G}}_0) = \Phi_3^!({\mathscr{G}}_0) = 0$.
nodes.statement_short: Generation: successive cones G_2, G_1, G_0

nodes.name: G_0 vanishes fiberwise, hence vanishes
nodes.statement: Then Lemma~\ref{lemma:phid-linear} implies that for any geometric point $s \in S$ setting ${\mathscr{G}}_{0s} = i_{X}^*({\mathscr{G}}_0) \in {\mathbf{D}}(X)$ to be the restriction of ${\mathscr{G}}_0$ to the fiber $X = {\mathscr{X}}_s$, we have $\Phi_d^!({\mathscr{G}}_{0s}) = 0$ for all $d$. By semiorthogonal decomposition~\eqref{eq:dbx-dz} this means that ${\mathscr{G}}_{0s} = 0$. Hence by Lemma~\ref{lemma:fiberwise}$(i)$ we have ${\mathscr{G}}_0 = 0$.
nodes.statement_short: G_0 vanishes fiberwise, hence vanishes

nodes.name: Chain proves the decomposition
nodes.statement: Thus we have a chain of morphisms \begin{equation*} {\mathscr{G}} =: {\mathscr{G}}_3 \to {\mathscr{G}}_2 \to {\mathscr{G}}_1 \to {\mathscr{G}}_0 = 0 \end{equation*} with $\mathrm{Cone}({\mathscr{G}}_{d} \to {\mathscr{G}}_{d-1}) \in \Phi_d({\mathbf{D}}({\mathscr{Z}}_d,\beta_{{\mathscr{Z}}_d}))$, which proves the required semiorthogonal decomposition.
nodes.statement_short: Chain proves the decomposition

nodes.name: S-linearity and base change compatibility
nodes.statement: This semiorthogonal decomposition is $S$-linear since by Lemma~\ref{lemma:phi-d-shriek} its embedding functors~$\Phi_d$ are $S$-linear, and its compatibility with base changes follows from~\cite[Theorem~6.4]{kuznetsov2011base} together with Lemma~\ref{lemma:phid-linear} and Lemma~\ref{lemma:md-zd-base-change}.
nodes.statement_short: S-linearity and base change compatibility

nodes.statement: The components of the semiorthogonal decomposition~\eqref{eq:sod-dp6} are admissible and their projection functors have finite cohomological amplitude. Moreover, the functors $\Phi_d$ preserve perfectness and induce a semiorthogonal decomposition \begin{equation} {\mathbf{D}}^{\mathrm{perf}}({\mathscr{X}}) = \langle \Phi_1({\mathbf{D}}^{\mathrm{perf}}(S)), \Phi_2({\mathbf{D}}^{\mathrm{perf}}({\mathscr{Z}}_2,\beta_{{\mathscr{Z}}_2})), \Phi_3({\mathbf{D}}^{\mathrm{perf}}({\mathscr{Z}}_3,\beta_{{\mathscr{Z}}_3})) \rangle. \end{equation}

nodes.name: Admissibility and perfect version of the family decomposition
conclusions: The components of the semiorthogonal decomposition~\eqref{eq:sod-dp6} are admissible and their projection functors have finite cohomological amplitude
nodes.label: proposition:sod-dp6-perfect-unbounded

nodes.statement: {\mathbf{D}}^{\mathrm{perf}}({\mathscr{X}}) = \langle \Phi_1({\mathbf{D}}^{\mathrm{perf}}(S)), \Phi_2({\mathbf{D}}^{\mathrm{perf}}({\mathscr{Z}}_2,\beta_{{\mathscr{Z}}_2})), \Phi_3({\mathbf{D}}^{\mathrm{perf}}({\mathscr{Z}}_3,\beta_{{\mathscr{Z}}_3})) \rangle.

nodes.name: Equation (52) sod-dpx-perf
nodes.label: eq:sod-dpx-perf

nodes.statement: The functor $\Phi_d$ has finite cohomological amplitude because the sheaf ${\mathscr{E}}_{{\mathscr{Z}}_d}$ is flat over ${\mathscr{Z}}_d$ by Lemma~\ref{lemma:ezd-tor-ext} (in fact, since $p \colon {\mathscr{X}} \times_S {\mathscr{Z}}_d \to {\mathscr{X}}$ is finite, the functor $\Phi_d$ is exact). The functor $\Phi_d^!$ has finite cohomological amplitude because the sheaf ${\mathscr{E}}_{{\mathscr{Z}}_d}$ has finite $\mathrm{Ext}$-amplitude over ${\mathscr{Z}}_d$ by Lemma~\ref{lemma:ezd-tor-ext} (in fact, since $p_d \colon {\mathscr{X}} \times_S {\mathscr{Z}}_d \to {\mathscr{Z}}_d$ is flat of relative dimension 2, the cohomological amplitude of the functor $\Phi_d^!$ equals $(0,2)$). Thus $\Phi_d \circ \Phi_d^!$ has finite cohomological amplitude. Since the projection functors of~\eqref{eq:sod-dp6} can be expressed as combinations of these functors (see the proof of Theorem~\ref{theorem:sod-dp6}), it follows that the projection functors also have finite cohomological amplitude. To show that the components of~\eqref{eq:sod-dp6} are admissible, note that we have two more decompositions \begin{equation} \begin{aligned} {\mathbf{D}}({\mathscr{X}}) &= \langle {\mathbf{D}}({\mathscr{Z}}_3,\beta_{{\mathscr{Z}}_3}) \otimes \omega_{{\mathscr{X}}/S}, {\mathbf{D}}(S), {\mathbf{D}}({\mathscr{Z}}_2, \beta_{{\mathscr{Z}}_2}) \rangle, \\ {\mathbf{D}}({\mathscr{X}}) &= \langle {\mathbf{D}}({\mathscr{Z}}_2, \beta_{{\mathscr{Z}}_2}) \otimes \omega_{{\mathscr{X}}/S}, {\mathbf{D}}({\mathscr{Z}}_3,\beta_{{\mathscr{Z}}_3}) \otimes \omega_{{\mathscr{X}}/S}, {\mathbf{D}}(S) \rangle. \end{aligned} \end{equation} Indeed, they can be established by the same argument as~\eqref{eq:sod-dp6} starting with the semiorthogonal decompositions~\eqref{eq:dbx-other} instead of~\eqref{eq:dbx}. Since $\omega_{{\mathscr{X}}/S}$ is invertible, the two above decompositions together with~\eqref{eq:sod-dp6} prove admissibility of all components (each of them appears on the left in one decomposition and on the right in another). The functors $\Phi_d$ preserve perfectness by Lemma~\ref{lemma:phi-d-shriek}. It remains to prove~\eqref{eq:sod-dpx-perf}. For this note that the functors $\Phi_d$ have left adjoints $\Phi_d^*$ because the components of~\eqref{eq:sod-dp6} are admissible. Since the functors $\Phi_d$ commute with arbitrary direct sums, it follows from~\cite[Theorem~5.1]{neeman1996grothendieck} that the functors $\Phi_d^*$ preserve perfectness. Since the projection functors of~\eqref{eq:sod-dp6} can be expressed as combinations of $\Phi_d \circ \Phi_d^*$, they preserve perfectness, hence a restriction of~\eqref{eq:sod-dp6} gives~\eqref{eq:sod-dpx-perf}.

nodes.statement: The relative duality functor gives a semiorthogonal decomposition \begin{equation} {\mathbf{D}}({\mathscr{X}}) = \langle {\mathrm{D}}_{{\mathscr{X}}/S}({\mathbf{D}}({\mathscr{Z}}_3,\beta_{{\mathscr{Z}}_3})), {\mathrm{D}}_{{\mathscr{X}}/S}({\mathbf{D}}({\mathscr{Z}}_2,\beta_{{\mathscr{Z}}_2})), {\mathrm{D}}_{{\mathscr{X}}/S}({\mathbf{D}}(S)) \rangle, \end{equation} whose components are equivalent to ${\mathbf{D}}({\mathscr{Z}}_3,\beta_{{\mathscr{Z}}_3})$, ${\mathbf{D}}({\mathscr{Z}}_2,\beta_{{\mathscr{Z}}_2})$, and ${\mathbf{D}}(S)$ respectively. Moreover, this decomposition is right mutation-dual to~\eqref{eq:sod-dp6}.

By base change together with Proposition~\ref{proposition:dbx-dual} and Lemma~\ref{lemma:fiberwise}, these two decompositions coincide. nodes.statement: Let ${\mathscr{X}} \to S$ be a du Val family of sextic del Pezzo surfaces. The total space ${\mathscr{X}}$ of the family is regular if and only if all three schemes $S$, ${\mathscr{Z}}_2$ and ${\mathscr{Z}}_3$ are regular.

nodes.statement: Consider decompositions~\eqref{eq:dbcx-again} and~\eqref{eq:sod-dpx-perf}. Indeed, this follows from Corollary~\ref{corollary:S-s} and the description of the fibers~$Z_d$ of ${\mathscr{Z}}_d \to S$ in Corollary~\ref{corollary:dbx-z2-z3}.

nodes.statement: Let ${\mathscr{X}} \to S$ and ${\mathscr{X}}' \to S$ be two du Val families of sextic del Pezzo surfaces with regular total spaces ${\mathscr{X}}$ and ${\mathscr{X}}'$. Assume there is a dense open subset $S_0 \subset S$ such that for some $d \in \{2,3\}$ there is an $S_0$-isomorphism $\varphi_0 \colon {\mathscr{Z}}_d({\mathscr{X}}_0/S_0) \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }{\mathscr{Z}}_d({\mathscr{X}}'_0/S_0)$, where ${\mathscr{X}}_0 = {\mathscr{X}} \times_S S_0$ and~${\mathscr{X}}'_0 = {\mathscr{X}}' \times_S S_0$. Then~$\varphi_0$ extends to an isomorphism $\varphi \colon {\mathscr{Z}}_d({\mathscr{X}}/S) \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ } {\mathscr{Z}}_d({\mathscr{X}}'/S)$ over $S$. Moreover, if we have an equality of Brauer classes $\beta_{{\mathscr{Z}}_d({\mathscr{X}}_0/S_0)} = \varphi_0^*\beta_{{\mathscr{Z}}_d({\mathscr{X}}'_0/S_0)}$ then it extends to $\beta_{{\mathscr{Z}}_d({\mathscr{X}}/S)} = \varphi^*\beta_{{\mathscr{Z}}_d({\mathscr{X}}'/S)}$.
nodes.name: Extension of isomorphisms of Z_d from a dense open subset
nodes.statement_short: For families with regular total spaces, an isomorphism of Z_d over a dense open subset extends over S, together with equality of Brauer classes.
