nodes.statement: Let ${{\mathscr{X}}_3} \subset {{\mathbb{X}}_3} \times {\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{V}}^\vee)$ be the universal hyperplane section of ${{\mathbb{X}}_3}$. By~\cite[Theorem~8.2]{kuznetsov2007hpd}, there is a semiorthogonal decomposition \begin{equation} {\mathbf{D}}({{\mathscr{X}}_3}) = \langle i_*\phi^*({\mathbf{D}}({{\mathbb{Y}}_3})), {\mathbf{D}}({\mathbb{P}}(V_1) \times {\mathbb{P}}(V_2) \times {\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{V}}^\vee)) \otimes {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_3}(1,1,1) \rangle, \end{equation} where the morphisms $i$ and $\phi$ are defined by the commutative diagram \begin{equation} \vcenter{\xymatrix{ {{\mathbb{Y}}_3} \times {\mathbb{P}}(V_3) \ar[r]^-i \ar[d]_\phi & {{\mathscr{X}}_3} \ar[d]^{p_{{\mathscr{X}}_3}} \\ {{\mathbb{Y}}_3} \ar[r]^-{p_{{\mathbb{Y}}_3}} & {\mathbb{P}}(V_1) \times {\mathbb{P}}(V_2) \times {\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{V}}^\vee) \ar[r] & {\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{V}}^\vee) }} \end{equation} and the map $p_{{\mathbb{Y}}_3}$ is induced by the embedding ${\mathscr{V}}_3^\perp \hookrightarrow {\mathbb{V}}^\vee \otimes {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{P}}(V_1) \times {\mathbb{P}}(V_2)}$. We modify~\eqref{eq:dbxx1} by a sequence of mutations to change it to the form we need. First, using the standard exceptional collection \begin{equation*} {\mathbf{D}}({\mathbb{P}}(V_1) \times {\mathbb{P}}(V_2)) = \langle {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{P}}(V_1) \times {\mathbb{P}}(V_2)}, {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{P}}(V_1) \times {\mathbb{P}}(V_2)}(1,0), {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{P}}(V_1) \times {\mathbb{P}}(V_2)}(0,1), {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{P}}(V_1) \times {\mathbb{P}}(V_2)}(1,1) \rangle \end{equation*} in ${\mathbf{D}}({\mathbb{P}}(V_1) \times {\mathbb{P}}(V_2))$, we rewrite \eqref{eq:dbxx1} as \begin{multline*} {\mathbf{D}}({{\mathscr{X}}_3}) = \langle i_*\phi^*({\mathbf{D}}({{\mathbb{Y}}_3})), {\mathbf{D}}({\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{V}}^\vee)) \otimes {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_3}(1,1,1), \\ {\mathbf{D}}({\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{V}}^\vee)) \otimes {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_3}(2,1,1), {\mathbf{D}}({\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{V}}^\vee)) \otimes {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_3}(1,2,1), {\mathbf{D}}({\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{V}}^\vee)) \otimes {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_3}(2,2,1) \rangle. \end{multline*} Mutating the last component to the far left, and taking into account that $\omega_{{\mathscr{X}}_3} \cong {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_3}(-1,-1,-1)$ up to a line bundle pulled back from ${\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{V}}^\vee)$, we get a semiorthogonal decomposition \begin{multline*} {\mathbf{D}}({{\mathscr{X}}_3}) = \langle {\mathbf{D}}({\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{V}}^\vee)) \otimes {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_3}(1,1,0), i_*\phi^*({\mathbf{D}}({{\mathbb{Y}}_3})), {\mathbf{D}}({\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{V}}^\vee)) \otimes {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_3}(1,1,1), \\ {\mathbf{D}}({\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{V}}^\vee)) \otimes {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_3}(2,1,1), {\mathbf{D}}({\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{V}}^\vee)) \otimes {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_3}(1,2,1) \rangle. \end{multline*} Next, mutating the second component to the left, we get \begin{multline*} {\mathbf{D}}({{\mathscr{X}}_3}) = \langle \Phi({\mathbf{D}}({{\mathbb{Y}}_3})), {\mathbf{D}}({\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{V}}^\vee)) \otimes {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_3}(1,1,0), {\mathbf{D}}({\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{V}}^\vee)) \otimes {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_3}(1,1,1), \\ {\mathbf{D}}({\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{V}}^\vee)) \otimes {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_3}(2,1,1), {\mathbf{D}}({\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{V}}^\vee)) \otimes {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_3}(1,2,1) \rangle. \end{multline*} where $\Phi = {\mathbb{L}}_{{\mathbf{D}}({\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{V}}^\vee)) \otimes {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_3}(1,1,0)} \circ i_* \circ \phi^* \colon {\mathbf{D}}({{\mathbb{Y}}_3}) \to {\mathbf{D}}({{\mathscr{X}}_3})$. Finally, mutating the second component to the far right and using the pullback of the standard exact sequence $0 \to {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{P}}(V_3)} \to V_3 \otimes {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{P}}(V_3)}(1) \to {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{P}}(V_3)}(2) \to 0$, we obtain \begin{multline} {\mathbf{D}}({{\mathscr{X}}_3}) = \langle \Phi({\mathbf{D}}({{\mathbb{Y}}_3})), {\mathbf{D}}({\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{V}}^\vee)) \otimes {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_3}(1,1,1), \\ {\mathbf{D}}({\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{V}}^\vee)) \otimes {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_3}(2,1,1), {\mathbf{D}}({\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{V}}^\vee)) \otimes {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_3}(1,2,1), {\mathbf{D}}({\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{V}}^\vee)) \otimes {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_3}(1,1,2) \rangle. \end{multline} As before, this almost proves the result. The only small thing left is to show that the functor $\Phi$ is a Fourier--Mukai functor whose kernel is supported on the fiber product ${{\mathbb{Y}}_3} \times_{{\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{V}}^\vee)} {{\mathscr{X}}_3}$. The same computations as in the proof of Theorem~\ref{theorem:hpd-p2p2} show that the functor~$\Phi$ fits into a distinguished triangle \begin{equation*} \Phi_{p_{{\mathbb{Y}}_3}^*({\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{P}}(V_1) \times {\mathbb{P}}(V_2)}(-1,-1)) \boxtimes p_{{\mathscr{X}}_3}^*({\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{P}}(V_1) \times {\mathbb{P}}(V_2)}(1,1))} \to \Phi_{j_*{\mathscr{O}}_{{{\mathbb{Y}}_3} \times {\mathbb{P}}(V_3)}} \to \Phi, \end{equation*} with notation introduced in~\eqref{diagram:yy-cx}. Again, it follows that this triangle is associated (up to a twist and a rotation) with the standard exact sequence \begin{equation*} 0 \to {\mathscr{I}}_{{{\mathbb{Y}}_3} \times {\mathbb{P}}(V_3), {{\mathbb{Y}}_3} \times_{{\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{V}}^\vee)} {{\mathscr{X}}_3}} \to {\mathscr{O}}_{{{\mathbb{Y}}_3} \times_{{\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{V}}^\vee)} {{\mathscr{X}}_3}} \to j_*{\mathscr{O}}_{{{\mathbb{Y}}_3} \times {\mathbb{P}}(V_3)} \to 0, \end{equation*} hence the functor $\Phi$ is indeed a Fourier--Mukai functor with kernel \begin{equation} {\mathbb{E}}_3 := {\mathscr{I}}_{{{\mathbb{Y}}_3} \times {\mathbb{P}}(V_3), {{\mathbb{Y}}_3} \times_{{\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{V}}^\vee)} {{\mathscr{X}}_3}} \otimes (p_{{\mathbb{Y}}_3}^*({\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{P}}(V_1) \times {\mathbb{P}}(V_2)}(-1,-1)) \boxtimes p_{{\mathscr{X}}_3}^*({\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{P}}(V_1) \times {\mathbb{P}}(V_2)}(1,1))) \end{equation} and thus completes the proof of the theorem.
nodes.statement_short: Same as for P^2 x P^2: linear HPD, mutations, and identification of the kernel.

nodes.statement: The natural map ${{\mathbb{Y}}_3} \to {\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{V}}^\vee)$ is generically finite of degree 2, and its branch divisor is the Cayley quartic $\overline{\mathrm{O}}_6$ (see Section~\ref{subsection:p1p1p1}). Moreover, the fiber of this morphism is isomorphic to~${\mathbb{P}}^1$ over~${\mathrm{O}}_4$, and to a reducible conic over~${\mathrm{O}}_3$. In particular, ${{\mathbb{Y}}_3}$ provides a small resolution of singularities of the double cover ${\mathscr{D}}_{V_1,V_2,V_3}$ of~${\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{V}}^\vee)$ branched over~$\overline{\mathrm{O}}_6$.
nodes.name: Fibers of Y_3 over P(V^v)
nodes.label: remark:fibers-resolution-dvvv

nodes.statement: We could, of course, exchange the role of $V_i$ in the construction. Then we would get a slightly different homological projectively dual variety as the result, that is for each permutation ${\sigma} \in {\mathfrak{S}}_3$ we would get \begin{equation*} {\mathbb{Y}}_3^{\sigma} = {\mathbb{P}}_{{\mathbb{P}}(V_{{\sigma}(1)}) \times {\mathbb{P}}(V_{{\sigma}(2)})} \Big(V_{{\sigma}(3)}^\vee \otimes \Omega_{{\mathbb{P}}(V_{{\sigma}(1)} \otimes V_{{\sigma}(2)})}(1)\vert_{{\mathbb{P}}(V_{{\sigma}(1)}) \times {\mathbb{P}}(V_{{\sigma}(2)})}\Big). \end{equation*} Note that for each ${\sigma}$ the natural map ${\mathbb{Y}}_3^{\sigma} \to {\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{V}}^\vee)$ factors through a birational morphism onto the double cover ${\mathscr{D}}_{V_1,V_2,V_3}$ of~${\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{V}}^\vee)$ branched over $\overline{\mathrm{O}}_6$. They provide six small resolutions of singularities of~${\mathscr{D}}_{V_1,V_2,V_3}$, related to each other by flops, identifying their derived categories. So, the homological projectively dual of~${\mathbb{X}}_3$ as a category is unambiguously defined, but has six different geometric models~${\mathbb{Y}}_3^{\sigma}$, ${\sigma} \in {\mathfrak{S}}_3$, breaking down its inner symmetry.
nodes.name: Six geometric models of the HPD of (P^1)^3
